papers.abstract: Nonreciprocal interactions, which violate action-reaction symmetry, constitute a broadly applicable mechanism for generating nonequilibrium forces in active and driven systems. Here, we explore how such interactions remodel polymer conformations using a minimal model in which local strain along the backbone gives rise to nonreciprocal forces. We find that bending rigidity is the decisive control parameter: flexible polymers contract under activity, whereas semiflexible polymers display a non-monotonic response that ultimately yields extension. These large-scale conformational changes arise despite only weak shifts in local structural statistics. Instead, activity reassigns bond-orientational correlations along the contour, damping orientational memory in flexible chains while amplifying it in semiflexible ones. Collectively, our results show that bending rigidity governs how deformation-dependent nonreciprocal activity transmits across length scales, offering a mechanism to regulate the structure and mechanics of active filamentous matter.

papers.title: GingivitisSeg: A Public Dataset and Comparative Benchmark for Gingivitis Segmentation in Intraoral Images
papers.abstract: Gingivitis segmentation from intraoral photographs can support computer-assisted periodontal assessment, but pixel-level delineation remains challenging due to severe foreground-background class imbalance, low-contrast boundaries, and variations in illumination and anatomy. We introduce GingivitisSeg, a public benchmark comprising 961 intraoral images with pixel-level annotations of gingival inflammation and predefined training (672), validation (144), and test (145) partitions. Seven semantic segmentation model-backbone configurations were compared using standardized partitions, input resolution, and evaluation metrics. Controlled ablation experiments examined class-weighted cross-entropy loss, Dice loss, and auxiliary supervision. UPerNet with ResNet50 achieved the highest mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 76.49% and gingivitis IoU of 54.91%. However, differences from DeepLabV3+ with ResNet50 and SegFormer with MiT-B2 were not statistically significant after Holm correction. The evaluated optimization components improved performance when combined in the UPerNet-ResNet50 configuration. Further analyses showed that performance was associated with gingivitis region size and decreased under stronger image blur. The dataset, benchmark splits, and source code are available at https://github.com/zeynepozdemir/GingivitisSeg.

papers.title: Beyond Symmetry: Asymmetric Matching with Transformers for Collective Entity Resolution
papers.abstract: A core assumption of entity resolution (ER) is its symmetric nature, which rests on a principle so self-evident it borders on tautology: if a refers to the same object as b, then b must also refer to the same object as a. However, this global property of symmetry does not necessarily extend to each of the complex decision processes within ER systems. In cases involving vague or ambiguous information, enforcing symmetry can be detrimental to performance, an issue exemplified by the ``bad triplet problem''. This paper investigates the effects of input-order asymmetry within a collective ER framework that integrates distinct matching and clustering stages. The input order-aware matching stage utilizes pre-trained transformers to explicitly model and exploit asymmetry, making it possible to evaluate its effect on clustering performance across multiple benchmark datasets. Our results demonstrate that asymmetry is not only measurable but also introduces a significant skew in the final entity clusters, highlighting the need to re-evaluate supervised training methodologies for matchers, particularly the development of direction-aware training paradigms that can preserve, rather than neutralize, the inherent asymmetry in matching tasks.

papers.title: Probing Unknown Luttinger-Like Parameters and Band Structure in BAs: A 24-Band k.p and DFT Approach
papers.abstract: In this work, the electronic band structure and the unknown Luttinger-like parameters associated with the p-type conduction bands (CBs) of boron arsenide (BAs) are calculated and analyzed using both 24-band $k.p$ and density functional (DFT) theories. For the DFT study, Gaussian and plane-wave basis sets implemented in the CP2K code were used. Comparison with DFT and available experimental results shows that the 24-band k.p model accurately reproduces the known electronic properties of BAs. These results demonstrate that the 24-band k.p model accurately reproduces the electronic band structure and key band parameters over the investigated energy range. In addition, the 24-band $k.p$ Hamiltonian parameters are adjusted and we show that the effective masses and the band parameters are validated against previously published theoretical studies. These findings suggest that the $k.p$ method is computationally more efficient than DFT, making it suitable for modeling complex nanostructures and quantum wells based on BAs semiconductor.

papers.title: OT-BLS: Optimal-Transport-based Backbone Layer Selection for Frozen DINOv3 in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
papers.abstract: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment a target class in images from a previously unseen domain using only a few annotated support examples. Training-free CD-FSS methods, which typically leverage vision foundation models such as DINOv3, achieve competitive performance without parameter updates. However, the optimal DINOv3 layer for mask prediction varies across support--query episodes. Although several layer-selection criteria have been proposed, they do not explicitly evaluate whether the predicted query foreground and background labels agree with the corresponding support labels. To address this limitation, we propose a novel layer-selection criterion, Optimal-Transport-Based Backbone Layer Selection (OT-BLS). Our key insight is that an effective layer-selection criterion can be derived from the optimal-transport correspondence between query and support patch-token features. Based on this insight, we first estimate the transport plan using a well-established optimal transport algorithm and then compute a layer-selection score by aggregating the transported mass according to the foreground--background partition defined by each candidate query mask. The resulting score reflects how well the predicted foreground and background of the query correspond to those of the support. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of OT-BLS. It outperforms the conventional last-layer baseline in 12 of 16 dataset/shot settings. Furthermore, OT-BLS improves the average mIoU from 55.72 to 57.62 and achieves a 2.99-point improvement over the best-performing existing layer-selection criterion while running 3.7--14.6$\times$ faster.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function
papers.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $Λ$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

papers.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
papers.abstract: Document editing is among the most common knowledge-work tasks, yet existing benchmarks for evaluating autonomous agents on Word document editing provide fully specified attribute-modification instructions. They do not evaluate agents' ability to infer the appropriate attributes from document context, a capability essential in real-world editing where users expect consistency without spelling out every attribute. We introduce WordInferBench, a benchmark comprising 280 base document-editing instances, each paired with three instruction conditions: descriptive (the instruction explicitly lists every attribute change), referential (the instruction points to another object as an exemplar), and inferential (the agent must examine document context to infer what attributes to apply). To evaluate contextual attribute inference, each base instance is constructed so that the target formatting is recoverable from an in-document exemplar. The instances are derived from real Word documents collected from Common Crawl and cover 13 object types and 81 attributes. We evaluate six recent coding-agent systems and find that the best-performing evaluated system, Claude Code with Opus 4.6, achieves a 62.9% task-level pass rate on descriptive variants but only 40.7% on inferential variants, indicating that current systems complete tasks less reliably when the required formatting changes must be determined from document context.

papers.title: Structural Analysis of Object-Valued Time Series
papers.abstract: We develop inference for structural patterns in the temporal association of object-valued time series. Our framework is built on pairwise lag profiles, which record the expected value of a chosen pairwise function at each lag and serve as a unified inferential target. We consider three representative structural features: whether a profile reaches stability beyond a finite lag, remains constant over time, and displays geometric regularity at short lags. To assess these properties, we design statistical tests calibrated by a common block multiplier bootstrap that accommodates serial dependence and the overlap inherent in lagged pairs. Gaussian approximation results establish bootstrap validity for asymptotic size control, while suitable signal conditions guarantee consistency against the corresponding alternatives. Finite-sample performance is examined through simulations in both Euclidean and density-valued settings. Applications to electricity load curves and stock-return distributions illustrate how the proposed procedures characterize association across lags.

papers.title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
papers.abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(Δ=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+Δ)\) is nef and big, then \((X,Δ)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata. We construct such a curve from a free Campana curve by attaching to it free rational curves which intersect positively with divisors that span the cone of effective divisors, and smooth the resulting comb.

papers.title: Interface-Driven Remote-Surface States in Rhombohedral Graphene
papers.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts low-energy states on its two outer surfaces. We identify a layer-by-layer mechanism through which a low-energy state generated at one surface acquires weight on successive layers up to the opposite surface. For an outer-layer vacancy, the wavefunction spreads over a larger area on successive layers, shifting normalized weight toward the remote surface as the system size increases. The same relation governs the extension of sublattice-polarized zero modes bound to circular voids and straight zigzag terminations. At periodic moire interfaces, it acts separately on each momentum harmonic, making the layer polarization of the low-energy bands depend on Bloch momentum and modulation period. This provides an intrinsic single-particle explanation for the remote-surface modulations observed in recent multilayer graphene experiments.

papers.title: Simplicity of the Three-Loop Six-Point ABJM Amplitude
papers.abstract: We compute the three-loop six-point amplitude in planar ABJM theory using negative geometries. At this order, only a single bipartite chain contributes to the logarithm of the amplitude, and we find that its dual-conformally invariant integrand is locally finite. The integrated chain is therefore infrared finite and, remarkably, equals exactly $-π^2$ times the one-loop amplitude. Hence the collinear anomalous dimension, like the cusp, receives no three-loop correction. Restoring the disconnected products of lower-loop contributions, which carry all the infrared divergences, we obtain the full three-loop amplitude, fixed entirely by lower-loop data and the coefficient $-π^2$. These results reveal an unexpected simplicity of the six-point ABJM amplitude and suggest an iterative relation between its odd- and even-loop terms.

papers.title: The Neighbour's Label: Opposite Subgroup Effects of Same-Dialogue Exposure in Next-Act Evaluation
papers.abstract: Window-based next-act evaluation often aims to measure generalisation across dialogues, yet overlapping windows and similarity retrieval can expose labelled examples from the test dialogue. The nearest such example is the target's labelled predecessor, whose act is correct when the target continues it and wrong when the target changes act; a model that copies it can gain and lose in two subgroups that one aggregate averages. We induce this exposure under controlled designs on SGD, STAR and AMI, whose official splits are clean. Randomly including the predecessor's row in training raises a lexical classifier's continuation scores and lowers its transition scores in all three corpora, and purging the adjacent rows removes most of the gain. With TF-IDF-retrieved demonstrations, two 7B instruction-tuned models show the same opposite pattern in all eight model-corpus-sample arms (some single-cell intervals include zero; one replication is partial), while natural-weight accuracy changes by only -0.05 to +0.04. Exposure frequency depends on the retrieval pipeline. We evaluate two diagnostic comparisons without model retraining and find that excluding the test dialogue does not detectably reduce accuracy on SGD. All exposure is induced; no published system was re-evaluated.

papers.title: A General Concept-based Decomposition for Vision-Language Embeddings
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models are designed to capture the compositional structure of the world through multi-modal alignment; however, it remains unclear whether their representations truly align with the way a human would naturally describe the same visual input. Prior works attempt to decompose visual embeddings into their concept-level contributions, but their instance-level optimization is inherently local and does not capture the model's global semantic structure, which is essential for compositional generalization across different inputs, tasks, and domains. We introduce GRACE, a method that learns this concept-based structure at the feature space level, producing semantic and general concept decompositions. To achieve this, we propose a novel training objective that preserves the geometric relations of different samples in the concept space, enabling a better understanding of how concepts compose and relate to each other. We validate GRACE on several image and video benchmarks, showing that its concept decomposition is aligned with human perception and achieves faithful decompositions across different tasks and domains. With minimal overhead, GRACE makes existing Vision-Language Models more interpretable, while preserving most of their original performance.

papers.title: The Calderón Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $ρ\in C^1(\overlineΩ)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-Δ+P^2ρ-ω^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-Δ+P^2ρ$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Empirical Likelihood Inference from LLM Annotations with Adaptive Human Auditing
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate unlabeled data as a fast, low-cost alternative to human annotation. However, their outputs can be biased and miscalibrated relative to human labels, potentially leading to misleading analysis and inference. We propose AAELI (Adaptive Human Auditing and Anytime-Valid Empirical Likelihood Inference), an online framework for estimating the population mean of human labels under a limited auditing budget. AAELI uses LLM outputs to guide adaptive human auditing and combines them with audited labels through predictable empirical-likelihood $e$-processes to construct anytime-valid confidence sequences. Our main theoretical result shows that a predictably learned efficient projection preserves the first-order profile empirical-likelihood statistic under adaptive auditing, without requiring a prescribed convergence rate for the projection estimator. This yields an exactly anytime-valid betting construction whose continuous-mixture form incurs a scalar rather than vector-dimensional mixing penalty. Supporting results establish adaptive empirical-likelihood asymptotics and show that a learned audit rule attains the oracle variance within the stated class of augmented estimating-equation designs under the same audit-probability floor and long-run expected budget. Experiments on synthetic data and three real-world datasets demonstrate that AAELI maintains empirical anytime coverage while requiring fewer human audits than the strongest competing baseline to reach a target precision.

papers.title: Dissipaton-embedded quantum master equation for nonlinear system-bath coupling
papers.abstract: The dissipaton theory was proposed more than a decade ago as a statistical quasiparticle theory for open quantum systems and was soon extended to nonlinear system-bath coupling. Although numerical results provided strong evidence for its validity, a rigorous mathematical foundation, particularly for nonlinear system-bath coupling, was established only recently. On this basis, we formulate the dissipaton-embedded quantum master equation for nonlinear system-bath coupling. This in-principle exact master equation describes the joint dynamics of the reduced system and all dissipaton degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.

papers.title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
papers.abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge $4s^2$ lone pair drives polar $B$-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn$^{2+}$ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between $x=0.60$ and $0.65$ that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic $Cc$ phase from a monoclinic $P2_1$ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

papers.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication Exponent 1.5 in the Low-bandwidth Model
papers.abstract: We study sparse matrix multiplication in the low-bandwidth model: $n$ computers multiply two $n\times n$ matrices, and each computer can send and receive one $O(\log n)$-bit message per round. The input matrices are uniformly sparse, meaning that there are at most $d$ nonzero entries in each row and column, and the task is to compute a uniformly sparse part of their product. In prior work, Gupta et al.~(SPAA 2022) presented an $O(d^{1.907})$-round algorithm over fields for this problem when the sparsity structure is globally known in advance (this is referred to as the supported setting). The upper bound was later improved to $O(d^{1.832})$ rounds. In this work, we give a deterministic algorithm that solves this problem in $O(d^{3/2})$ rounds in the supported setting, improving the previous bounds over fields and semirings.

papers.title: Transient CFD simulation of a linear start-up of a variable speed reversible pump-turbine
papers.abstract: The integration of intermittent energy sources has led to a growing demand for fast response and partial-load operation of hydraulic turbines, making variable speed units increasingly important. In hydraulic turbines, frequent start-stop cycles generate the highest loads under normal operating conditions. Although historically infrequent and often neglected in turbine design, the growing occurrence of these cycles now necessitates particular consideration due to their contribution to fatigue loading and reduced runner lifetime. Experimental investigations of turbine start-up are costly and cannot be conducted during early design stages. While start-up sequences have been simulated with CFD for fixed speed turbines, each approach has had notable limitations. Some studies have lacked experimental validation. Some studies have used reduced geometrical domains, making it unclear whether inaccuracies stem from geometry simplification or turbulence modelling, and others employ hybrid LES/RANS models, at a very high computational cost, making them unfeasible for use during the design phase. In this study, the linear start-up of a variable-speed turbine start-up is simulated using URANS-based approaches. Simulations are performed using the k-$ω$ SST, EARSM, and the RSM turbulence models within a computationally tractable framework. The simulations show that torque, mass flow, and the blade-passing frequency content at the leading edge are accurately captured by all models. In contrast, the frequency content at the trailing edge and in the draft tube is considerably better resolved using the RSM than the other models because of its capability to consistently capture turbulence anisotropy.

papers.title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
papers.abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

papers.title: Alignment De-Identifies Without Aligning: A Congruence-Invariant Relational Gap in Cross-Subject Neural Representations
papers.abstract: In brain-computer interfaces, inter-subject variability remains a major challenge that limits decoding performance across users. Subject-wise alignment is widely used to improve cross-subject transfer of neural decoders, yet it is typically evaluated only through decoding accuracy, which cannot determine whether aligned representations share greater task-related structure. We therefore distinguish two questions that accuracy conflates: whether alignment removes subject-specific information and whether it makes the relational organization of task conditions more similar across individuals. Using three motor imagery-EEG cohorts, trials are represented as covariance matrices and aligned by recentering each subject's mean covariance to a common reference. Subject-specific information is quantified with a subject-identification probe, whereas relational structure is assessed using representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs) computed from condition means with the affine-invariant Riemannian distance. We show that recentering leaves this distance, and therefore the resulting RDMs, unchanged. Consistent with this result, recentering reduces subject identification accuracy from 0.96 to chance level across all cohorts, while altering RDMs only at numerical precision. Cross-subject agreement in relational structure is significantly above zero but below the estimator's lower noise ceiling. Introducing an explicit similarity regularizer during training also fails to increase held-out agreement: the apparent reduction in between-subject differences is explained by a decline in the reliability ceiling rather than improved alignment. These findings show that eliminating subject identity is not equivalent to aligning relational geometry. More broadly, alignment claims must be interpreted relative to the invariances of both the distance and the statistic used to evaluate them.

papers.title: Algorithms for Robust Dedicated Actuator Placement
papers.abstract: We study dedicated actuators installed at distinct states of a structured linear system. Failures remove actuators but preserve states and state arcs. For unit costs and one failure, an exact source-quota relaxation followed by maximum matching in a \emph{common-repair graph} yields a $3/2$-approximation on arbitrary directed state graphs using $O(n^3)$ elementary graph operations. The analysis combines fundamental cocircuit unions with the Tutte--Berge formula. For multiple failures, we give an exact algorithm fixed-parameter tractable in the maximum-matching deficiency and failure budget, independently of the number of source strongly connected components. The underlying result solves resilient matroid spanning with an arbitrary number of disjoint unit-cost quota constraints. We also establish an exact weighted spanning algorithm for safe and vulnerable elements in the independence-oracle model, with an application to strongly connected state graphs.

papers.title: Astrometric effects of anisotropic gravitational wave backgrounds
papers.abstract: Precise astrometric observations of distant objects such as stars and quasars can be used to probe gravitational wave signals at nanohertz frequencies. A stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) produces correlated apparent motions of pairs of objects on the sky. That correlation as a function of their angular separation is the astrometric analog of the Hellings-Downs curve in the context of pulsar timing measurements. Upper limits on the SGWB have been obtained from very-long baseline interferometry and Gaia astrometry, and future Gaia data releases are expected to improve them. An astrophysical background from inspiraling supermassive black hole binaries is expected to be significantly anisotropic. In this work, we compute the astrometric correlation functions for an anisotropic SGWB, known as the generalized overlap reduction functions, for all six gravitational wave polarizations. We present closed-form expressions in all cases where the distant-light source limit can be applied, following the approach used for pulsar timing arrays. We find that the correlations differ qualitatively between the tensor, vector, and scalar polarizations. Finally, we discuss the applicability of these results in future astrometry searches for arbitrarily polarized anisotropic gravitational wave backgrounds.

papers.title: Pre-QED: Environment Specifications for Agentic Verification
papers.abstract: LLM agents are making formal verification practical at scale. Recently, many attempts have raised this as an enticing possibility. However, formal verification at scale is only meaningful if deep formal specifications capturing functionality are available for checking. Unfortunately, recent works seek to bypass this issue by using shallow specifications devised for purposes other than verification. OSS-Verify from Anthropic and Theorem, for example, reuses the fuzz harnesses of open-source libraries as specifications and has an agent prove that each harness never crashes. However, a fuzz harness follows a single sequence of API calls under a single calling context, so the resulting proof covers one usage scenario rather than the library. We argue that the bottleneck of agentic verification has shifted from how to prove to what to prove. Before zooming into verification at scale, we need deep environment specifications to prove, which is why we call our effort Pre-QED. We propose verification harnesses, executable harnesses that model all legal usages of an API, so that a proof about the harness is a proof about every well-behaved client. To construct them, we use an agentic workflow that extracts the API's usage contract from code / documentation, and uses Linear-time Temporal Logic (LTL) to rule out illegal call orders. We identify the challenges in proving verification harnesses and release our harnesses open-source as challenges for the community. The overarching vision is that verifying an open-source library should become as routine as fuzzing it, with a guarantee that covers every well-behaved client rather than a single scenario like a fuzzing harness.

papers.title: Analytic T-Matrix Formalism for Helmholtz Resonators
papers.abstract: We develop an analytic T-matrix formalism for two-dimensional circular acoustic Helmholtz resonators with thin rigid walls. The central idea is to use an aperture projection operator to obtain a compact expression for the T-matrix with explicit coefficients describing coupling and decoupling between external fields and cavity resonances. An equivalent formulation providing much faster convergence uses an aperture-to-Fourier map and an edge-adapted basis for the aperture flux. The method extends directly to multiple apertures of arbitrary angular widths and positions. The calculated scattering spectra agree with full-wave numerical simulations. For single- and double-aperture resonators, we decompose the T-matrix into even and odd parts under inversion to identify the channels associated with Willis coupling. We show how internal losses enable direction-dependent scattering and absorption when inversion symmetry is broken, while reciprocity ensures equal extinction for opposite incidence. Finally, we show how shifting the expansion origin redistributes radiation among multipole channels, enabling more compact T-matrix representations.

papers.title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
papers.abstract: We prove that the collection of all cluster boundaries of near-critical site percolation (with a fixed parameter) on the triangular lattice has a unique scaling limit in the loop-ensemble space, as the mesh size tends to 0. This answers a problem proposed by Camia, Fontes and Newman (2006). Using this, we also prove that near-critical percolation exploration path in a disk converges in distribution to a continuous path as the mesh size goes to 0. The main idea of our proof is to construct the cut-off loop ensembles under the near-critical coupling, based on the enhanced networks and the quad-crossing scaling limits of near-critical percolation constructed by Garban, Pete and Schramm (2018); the proof also relies on the study of the geometry of cluster chains. Some properties of the limiting loop ensemble, including rotation invariance, scale covariance and finite chaining, are established. Moreover, a few applications of our scaling-limit result and proof strategy are discussed.

papers.title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constants
papers.abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge2$ that is not a power of two there are constants $c_n>0$ and $B_n>2$ such that $s(C_n^r)\ge c_nB_n^r$ for all $r\ge1$. For powers of two, Harborth's formula gives growth rate exactly $2$. For the remaining even exponents, the previous lower bounds were of order $r2^r$. When $n=2m$ with $m\ge3$ odd, we prove the transfer inequality \[ A_n(H\oplus C_n^5)\ \ge\ 12\,A_n(H\oplus C_n)+8\,A_n(H\oplus C_m), \] where $A_n(G)$ is the maximal length of a sequence over $G$ without an $n$-term zero-sum subsequence and $H$ is any finite abelian group whose exponent divides $n$. The transfer extends a configuration of Elsholtz to twenty full cyclic fibers. Combined with a nine-point binary construction for $2m$-term zero-sums over $C_m^r$, it gives bases at least $2.0341$ that tend to $2.0394\ldots$; combined with a finite-field construction, it gives $s(C_6^r)\ge c\cdot 2.0491^r$. For exponents divisible by $4$ that are not powers of two, we obtain a base above two from a weighted random construction on the eighteen-point configuration of Wang and Zeng.

papers.title: Least Expensive Standard Pensions
papers.abstract: The paper proposes generating annuity payment streams at far lower costs than those implied by traditional theories. For a given investment universe, this enables the design of a least expensive standard pension, providing accurate monthly payments of savings account units over a set period. Such a standard pension invests dynamically in the savings account and the equity market's growth-optimal portfolio to replicate riskless payments with high accuracy at the lowest possible cost. Since this mathematically grounded standard pension is reliable and, by orders of magnitude, less expensive than traditional pensions, it provides a unique opportunity to improve the health of pension systems and provide more benefits for retirees.

papers.title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,dμ=0 \] for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis. We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if \[ \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,dμ= O(r^d) \] for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.

papers.title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
papers.abstract: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.

papers.title: Chirality-Odd Readout of Coherence-Mediated Magnon Spin Transport
papers.abstract: Structural chirality is ubiquitous in magnets, yet its impact on spin transport in insulators remains largely unexplored, with only a few recent experiments offering the first glimpses. Here we predict the chiral response in the electric spin injection-detection configuration in both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic spirals. The screw symmetry of the spiral forbids any nonzero diagonal element of the magnon spin matrix: every eigenmode is linearly polarized and carries no spin, so spin transport is mediated entirely by superposition between distinct modes. Reversing chirality flips the magnon spin along the spiral axis and the injected quantum coherence in lockstep, leaving the associated injected spin current invariant. Spiral chirality acts instead at the detection interface, where electron--magnon scattering amplitude is reversed and causes the magnon accumulation to be read out as a voltage of opposite sign. This interfacial readout is consistent with reversed first-harmonic voltage under electric-field switching in multiferroic BiFeO$_3$, establishing structural chirality as an intrinsic control parameter for magnon coherence and its electrical readout.

papers.title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
papers.abstract: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retaining the adapted dynamics without new observations so that later predictions do not revert to the old dynamics. Inspired by predictive coding in the human brain with multi-timescale adaptation, we propose AFTER-WM, a world model with Adaptive Fast-slow Timescales for Error-driven Retention, whose prediction errors drive a fast correction that fades and a slow correction that persists, while dynamically adjusting the combination weights of pre-trained experts without altering them, to overcome the trade-offs among responsiveness, stability and persistence. On five simulated robot datasets and real UAV data, AFTER-WM has a lower multi-step mean error than all ten compared models and the highest mean return in a joint-failure control task. In simulation, its multistep mean error is 16%-34% below the strongest compared model's and is also the lowest 1-4 steps after a change and under transient disturbances alone, and its step-40 error is the lowest as well, reflecting responsiveness, stability and persistence. All code (method, baselines, experiments) and datasets will be released online.

papers.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: \textbf{Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS)} aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prompt. We trace this to a recall bottleneck rather than a mask-quality one, and address it with a training-free, modular system. The pipeline first generates high-recall object proposals using an off-the-shelf class-agnostic detector, then matches each proposal to the reference using foundation-model features (e.g., BLIP-2), and finally refines the selected box with SAM. For robust matching we propose \textbf{top-$K$ Sinkhorn}, a patch-level distance that scores each candidate only on its most confidently matched patches; trimming the Sinkhorn dual potentials recovers the robustness of partial optimal transport at more than $100\times$ lower cost, keeping it inside the per-proposal candidate loop. To evaluate this regime, we introduce \textbf{\datasetname}, a realistic multi-instance benchmark. Across \datasetname, PerSeg, PerMIS, and DAVIS, our system surpasses PerSAM, $\mathrm{P}^2\mathrm{SAM}$, and PDM by up to $\sim\!48$ mIoU while matching their runtime and using fewer parameters, establishing a strong, deployable training-free baseline for real-world personalized segmentation.

papers.title: Are We Ready for Snow-tonomous Driving? Challenges Toward Robust Automated Driving in Extreme Weather
papers.abstract: Automated driving has gained remarkable momentum over the past decade, with both industry and academia investing substantial resources in developing perception and control solutions to advance vehicle autonomy. However, these efforts have largely focused on clear-weather scenarios, leaving harsh conditions, such as snow, rain, and fog, comparatively understudied. As a result, inclement weather remains one of the most significant hurdles for autonomous vehicles, often leading to substantial performance degradation in downstream perception and control tasks. In this paper, we present insights from the EU-funded Horizon Europe project ROADVIEW, which aims to develop robust, weather-aware perception and control modules for connected and automated vehicles operating under severe conditions, including snow, rain, and fog. Drawing on four years of large-scale development and real-world demonstrations across multiple vehicle platforms in different locations, we identify ten key challenges that hinder the development of weather-resilient autonomy, including data scarcity, domain shifts, limitations in multimodal perception, control robustness, and validation gaps, among others. We summarize these challenges and lessons learned toward enabling reliable snow-autonomous driving, highlighting critical directions for future research and standardization.

papers.title: Enhancing Graviton--Photon Conversion through Galactic Magnetic Turbulence
papers.abstract: Plasma dispersion suppresses coherent graviton-photon conversion over astrophysical distances. We show that Galactic magnetic turbulence enables phase matching by compensating the plasma-induced mismatch, allowing matched magnetic modes to contribute coherently. In the long path limit, the ensemble-averaged conversion probability grows linearly with propagation distance in the phase matched regime and is governed by the projected magnetic power spectrum. Applied to photon background observations, this mechanism yields characteristic strain limits that are stronger than previous Galactic conversion bounds in the inertial range phase matching window, with improvements of up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: A Multi-Parent Edge Assembly Crossover Driven Hybrid Genetic Algorithm for the Hamiltonian \textit{p}-Median Problem
papers.abstract: The Hamiltonian \textit{p}-median problem seeks to partition the vertices of a graph into exactly $p$ disjoint cycles while minimizing their total cost. This paper presents a hybrid genetic algorithm incorporating a multi-parent edge assembly crossover operator. The crossover combines a base solution with multiple donor solutions in a single recombination operation, thereby expanding the space of available edge exchanges. It uses virtual copies of the base solution to establish edge balance, together with an auxiliary directed graph and a budgeted search to construct valid AB-cycles. Extensive experiments on 215 benchmark instances across four sets show that the proposed algorithm improves the best-known solution values for 34 instances and matches those for another 168. Additional experiments indicate that a moderate number of parents provides beneficial diversity, whereas excessive parent counts, particularly when $p$ is large, lead to excessive population dispersion and hinder convergence.

papers.title: FréchetFlow: Flow Matching for Non-Euclidean Data
papers.abstract: Scientific observations such as probability distributions, trees and covariance matrices call for generative models that respect their non-Euclidean geometry. While flow matching has been extended to manifolds by utilizing geodesics and velocities, such manifold structures are not available in a general metric space. We introduce FréchetFlow, a generative modeling framework for metric space-valued data that requires neither linear operations nor a smooth manifold structure. A key feature of the proposed approach is that we utilize well-established Euclidean flows to learn the joint distribution of distances to a set of landmarks, whereupon new objects are reconstructed from generated landmark representations. The reconstruction step utilizes weighted Fréchet means of reference objects, drawing on Fréchet regression. We establish Wasserstein error bounds that connect accuracy of the generated object distributions to the placement of landmarks, flow approximation and reconstruction error and prove consistency under finite second moments. This leads to convergence rates that depend on the metric complexity of the target objects, tail moments and fitting accuracy. Experiments show competitive accuracy with established flow matching methods in Euclidean simulations and lower Wasserstein errors than specifically tailored methods for several scientific datasets. Across simulation settings, we find that generation error decreases as sample size increases.

papers.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
papers.abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

papers.title: Improvements in Tropical Cyclone Representation in JRA-3Q over ERA5
papers.abstract: Reanalysis products are widely used for long-term tropical cyclone (TC) studies, yet the fidelity of their TC representation is not fully established. We evaluate TC representation in the recently released JRA-3Q reanalysis against the higher-resolution ERA5 using the SyCLoPS tracker. JRA-3Q achieves substantially higher detection skill, with a hit rate of 90% and a false alarm rate of 6% during 1979-2024. Unlike ERA5, which exhibits markedly degraded detection skill during the pre-satellite era, JRA-3Q maintains stable performance over time. We analyze false alarms and missed TCs in the North Indian basin, TC vortex evolution following TC bogussing, and the spatial variance of column-integrated moist static energy, showing that JRA-3Q's improvements stem from both reduced model biases and a more effective and consistently applied TC bogus scheme. A decomposition of TC representation errors into contributions from tracking algorithm, reanalysis, and best-track uncertainty helps explain the sources of these biases.

papers.title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Large-language model (LLM) agents execute actions on external systems through tool calls, and enterprises deploy runtime controls, such as agent gateways, to check this behavior in real time. However, a control can only evaluate the actions that cross the point where it is placed, and an agent can act through more paths than the tool-call channel; no existing work measures this coverage against kernel-level ground truth. In this paper, we present guardscope, a framework that makes this coverage measurable. guardscope works in two stages: a static stage that predicts which of an agent's 15 action paths a control can check from its source, and an empirical stage that runs a fixed workload on a deployment that realizes one of eight topology designs and classifies every executed action as checked, bypassed, or prevented by reconciling the control's decision records against kernel-level ground truth. guardscope makes a control's coverage claim verifiable: a runtime control developer can publish which paths its product inspects under a kernel-verified protocol. We conducted experiments with two agent harnesses and real runtime controls, including Microsoft's agent governance toolkit and agentgateway. guardscope is available at https://github.com/VulcanLab/guardscope.

papers.title: DGPExplainer: Generating Prototype Sequence Explanations for Dynamic Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been successfully applied to learning from graph-structured data. However, applying them to dynamic graphs-where nodes and edges evolve over time-presents significant challenges, particularly regarding explainability. While explanation techniques for static GNNs are well established, they do not readily extend to dynamic GNNs (DGNNs) due to the added complexity introduced by temporal dynamics and spatiotemporal dependencies, especially when generating model-level explanations. To address this gap, we introduce DGPExplainer, a post-hoc, prototype-based explainer specifically designed for DGNN models that transforms their complex decision-making processes into human-understandable, analogical, case-based explanations. DGPExplainer first employs local explanation methods to identify important elements within temporal snapshots of dynamic graph sequences. It then decomposes the graph at each time step into distinct prototypes, thereby symbolizing the dynamic graph sequence. Finally, we design a sequence generation method that uses these symbolized sequences to learn and generate class-specific dynamic graph pattern sequences that serve as prototype explanations. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method effectively produces prototype-based explanations for DGNN models across multiple classes.

papers.title: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
papers.abstract: Surround-view video understanding in autonomous driving is a crucial capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve reliable driving reasoning. Real-world driving often requires information beyond the front-view camera. Existing MLLMs primarily focus on front-view information, while their spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning abilities remain unknown. To address this gap, we propose MVDriveBench, a high-information-density video QA benchmark for autonomous driving, characterized by synchronized surround-view inputs, spatio-temporal understanding, and reasoning-chain-oriented evaluation. We design 12 categories of QA tasks that cover the complete reasoning pipeline from low-level visual perception to high-level driving decision-making, enabling a systematic evaluation of MLLMs surround-view spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning capabilities in complex driving environments. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 23 open-source, closed-source, and expert MLLMs on MVDriveBench. The results show that current MLLMs still exhibit insufficient surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning ability. Meanwhile, closed-loop evaluations of specialist models in AlpaSim reveal a correlation between surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning capabilities and closed-loop driving performance, highlighting the importance of comprehensive multi-view understanding for reliable vehicle control.

papers.title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
papers.abstract: We investigate the potential nuclear de-excitation $γ$-ray line emission from low-energy cosmic rays (LECRs) in the Vela SNR region, one of the nearest and most angularly extended core-collapse supernova remnant (SNR) complexes. We calculate the MeV line emission from Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A using the TALYS nuclear reaction code, considering both direct and inverse interactions between the accelerated particles and the nuclei interior to the SNRs. The proton spectra are constrained by GeV--TeV $γ$-ray observations under the hadronic assumption, while a broad range of spectral indices is explored to account for the poorly constrained LECR population. We find that Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs. The integrated fluxes of the prominent 1.63 MeV $^{20}$Ne, 4.44 MeV $^{12}$C and 6.13 MeV $^{16}$O lines are approximately $1.3\times10^{-10}$ -- $1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$ -- $5.6\times10^{-7}$ and $1.6\times10^{-10}$--$2.6\times10^{-7}$ $\rm ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}$, respectively, over the explored proton spectra. We compare the predicted line emission with both the diffuse Galactic MeV continuum and local source-related continuum emission. In our background estimate, diffuse Galactic emission is the dominant component, while inverse Compton emission from pulsar wind nebula Vela X constitutes an additional local continuum component. The relatively low diffuse background toward Vela compared with the Galactic Center makes this region a promising target for future MeV $γ$-ray observations. Such observations could provide direct constraints on the LECR population and particle acceleration in this complex SNR region.

papers.title: MOON-RL: Multi-Objective Optimization via Objective Space Navigation with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Many engineering design problems involve multiple conflicting objectives and strict feasibility constraints. They are typically solved with population-based optimizers that require many evaluations and offer limited online control over where the search is focused. We present MOON-RL, a reinforcement-learning-based optimization framework that formulates constrained multi-objective search as preference-directed navigation in the objective space. In MOON-RL, a lightweight PPO policy receives objective-space and constraint-related observations and acts as an instance-specific adaptive search process. It learns how to update the design so that the current solution advances along a user-specified trade-off direction, while a simple meta-algorithm periodically resets the policy, resamples starting designs from a continuously updated archive of non-dominated solutions, and adjusts step-size and penalty schedules. We evaluate MOON-RL on real-world actuator-design problems and additional convergence-hard constrained benchmarks, comparing against established evolutionary algorithms under matched evaluation budgets. In focused search scenarios, MOON-RL achieves competitive performance in the region of interest, and ablation studies show that both the RL-driven adaptive sampling process and the meta-algorithm contribute to this behaviour, suggesting that repurposing RL training as objective-space navigation is a viable building block for interactive, preference-guided design tools. Additional experiments show that the framework also accommodates adaptive non-RL samplers, while PPO remains a strong choice for fixed-target, preference-directed objective-space navigation.

papers.title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
papers.abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

papers.title: Trading Memory for Depth: Tight Bounds for LCU Block-Encodings
papers.abstract: An LCU block-encoding of $A=\sum_jα_j U_j$ runs the $U_j$ in series on one register, so its select depth is the total work $\sum_j d_j$. Depth was the one block-encoding constraint with no knob: grouping the $T$ terms into $g$ registers that run in parallel gives it one, and the binning is the knob. For a $g$-branched realisation (up to $g$ oracles in parallel) the select depth is tight at $Θ(C+\log(g\,\max\{n,m\}))$ for $g\ge2$, with $C$ the binning makespan and $m$ the largest bin, in the $k$-local atomic-oracle model. The work floor is a two-way reduction to classical multiprocessor scheduling: every realisation \emph{induces} a $g$-machine schedule, and the construction realises any binning, so an optimal binning attains it. The additive logarithmic routing term is a light-cone cost, independent of the selector encoding and robust to register reuse, measurement, reset, and teleportation; width is at least $gn$. The standard $1/α$ subnormalisation and success probability are unchanged; the endpoints are sequential LCU ($g{=}1$) and the fully parallel realisation ($g{=}T$). Allowing the oracles to be split (McNaughton's rule) reaches the work floor $\sum_j d_j/g$. Two selector realisations trade space for depth: a dense (Möttönen) one is memory-tight at the standard LCU footprint but its multiplexed controls cost a $\log\log(m{+}1)$ factor on the makespan; a one-hot one is depth-tight at $T$ selector qubits. Neither reaches both at once.

papers.title: UOCS. XVI. Census of post mass-transfer binaries across various evolutionary phases in M67
papers.abstract: M67 is a well-studied, solar-metallicity, old open cluster that hosts a diverse set of exotic stellar populations formed via mass transfer (MT). While Case A, B, and C MT systems have been individually examined in several clusters, a comprehensive investigation of all MT types across different evolutionary stages within a single cluster remains limited. This study aims to detect the presence of post mass-transfer systems using two different methods and thereby obtain a holistic view of binary evolution and mass-transfer mechanisms prevalent in M67. We constructed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for 141 UV-detected stars in M67 using far-UV data from AstroSat/UVIT, combined with archival data from Swift/UVOT, GALEX, Gaia, 2MASS, WISE, and other sources. Furthermore, we performed a detailed chemical abundance analysis of cluster members using high-resolution spectroscopy from the GALAH DR3+ survey. We identified 11 new MS+WD binaries with previously undetected hotter companions, effectively doubling the known MS+WD binary population in M67. This includes five confirmed ELM WDs with orbital periods of 100-200 days and no chemical peculiarities, confirming Case A or B post-MT systems. We also detected 13 long-period SB1 systems with orbital periods longer than 1000 days and enhancements in s-process elements (Ba, La, Y), indicating Case C post-MT systems enriched by thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companions which have evolved into undetected WDs. This study demonstrates that M67 hosts a diverse population of post-mass transfer binaries formed via Case A, B, and C mechanisms. The unified view makes M67 a key benchmark for studying binary star evolution and highlights the role of UV observations and high-resolution spectroscopy in uncovering hidden stellar histories.

papers.title: TQIR: Trellis Quantization with Integer Reconstruction for Bandwidth-Efficient Edge LLM Acceleration
papers.abstract: Autoregressive large language model (LLM) inference is often limited by external-memory bandwidth, while existing ultra-low-bit trellis quantization reconstructs floating-point weights and leaves runtime Hadamard-transform and decoder costs unresolved. This paper presents TQIR, an algorithm--hardware co-design that decouples storage precision ($S$) from decoded-weight ($W$) and activation ($A$) compute precisions, enabling a better accuracy--hardware trade-off. TQIR performs trellis matching with floating-point candidates offline while constraining each candidate to an INT8 or INT4 codeword that can be reproduced exactly for integer GEMM at runtime. To reduce transform cost while preserving the integer weight path, TQIR relocates the reverse Hadamard transform to the activation side and employs an $H_{128}$ Subspace Hadamard Transform, together with a subspace-aligned $128\times2$ trellis tile that preserves the original 256-weight sequence length. The configurable decoder, synthesized in a TSMC 16-nm process, delivers 307.2~Gweights/s in 0.0509~mm$^2$ and achieves 13.93$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ the normalized decoder-area efficiency of Ecco and Codeword Decomposition, respectively. These results show that fixed-rate trellis compression can reduce weight traffic while sustaining an integer-GEMM datapath matched to the evaluated memory and PE rates.

papers.title: Winter wheat improves soil carbon sequestration with reduced gains in warmer climates
papers.abstract: Sustainable agricultural intensification requires a precise understanding of how land use decisions influence soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration under varying environmental conditions. We apply causal machine learning to evaluate the heterogeneous impact of winter wheat-based rotations on SOC at the field-level across Lithuania. Using a nationwide dataset collected over five years (2018-2022), including crop types, management practices, soil properties, and environmental conditions, we estimate how the effects of winter wheat-based rotation vary across space and climate. Our results indicate that winter wheat generally enhances SOC levels, but its effectiveness is modulated by climate. Cooler regions experience higher SOC gains, whereas warmer regions show diminished or even negative effects. Future climate projections suggest that the potential for winter wheat carbon sequestration may decline under high-emission scenarios. These findings highlight the importance of localized agricultural strategies that account for climate variability to maximize SOC sequestration and ensure long-term soil sustainability.

papers.title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
papers.abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincaré map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

papers.title: Schedule-Calibrated Commitment Order in Blockwise Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Sequential block schedules can make token commitment in masked diffusion language models appear strongly left-to-right even when within-block order is random or reversed. For equal contiguous blocks processed without interleaving in positional order, with untied irreversible commitments, we use a Spearman-rank identity to express global position-commitment correlation as a deterministic schedule reference plus a weighted mean within-block correlation. In a reported paired study of LLaDA-8B-Instruct on 500 math and code prompts with 256 generated positions and updates, increasing block size from 64 to 128 lowers mean global correlation from 0.9845 to 0.9149. Uniform-random within-block references are already 0.9375 and 0.7500. After calibration, mean within-block correlations are 0.751 and 0.660, so the larger raw residual at block size 128 does not indicate stronger local positional ordering. We give sharp bounds and derive calibrated intervals from reported summaries, while documenting the limitations of the aggregate-only empirical release. The analysis supports schedule-aware interpretation of commitment order; its empirical scope is one checkpoint and two schedules, without evaluation of output quality or inference speed.

papers.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Physically Consistent Prediction of Mutual Diffusion Coefficients in Binary Liquid Mixtures
papers.abstract: Experimental data on mutual diffusion coefficients in liquid mixtures are scarce, and existing prediction methods are unreliable for non-ideal mixtures. Building on HADES, our hybrid model for self-diffusion coefficients, we introduce the Enhanced Vignes Equation (EVE), which augments the Vignes equation with a deep-set model. Its inputs are molecular descriptors derived from SMILES and activity-coefficient information from HANNA, a machine-learning model for activity coefficients. EVE predicts Maxwell--Stefan diffusion coefficients; the corresponding Fickian coefficients follow from the thermodynamic factor, likewise obtained from HANNA. Trained and evaluated on 2106 experimental data points for 123 binary mixtures, EVE outperforms all available semi-empirical models, halving the mean absolute relative error for mixtures without experimental infinite-dilution diffusion data. Combined with HADES, EVE yields the complete set of self- and mutual diffusion coefficients of a binary mixture from SMILES and pure-component viscosities alone. EVE and HADES are available at https://ml-prop.mv.rptu.de/, and the code is fully disclosed.

papers.title: Sub-100KB On-Device CNN Training via Dynamic Sparse Updates and Hardware--Software Co-Design
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for real-time processing and personalized deep learning has made edge-device training essential but challenging due to high memory and computational costs. To address this, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training accelerator with a dynamic sparse update mechanism that selectively updates important parameters using a random channel strategy, avoiding costly evaluations. Combined with activation pruning, our approach reduces activation storage to just 3.4\% of the original. Our hardware features a fused forward dataflow that concurrently processes group normalization and convolution, reducing training time by 45\% through computation reordering and efficient zero-skipping. Implemented in TSMC 28nm at FP8 precision, the design operates at 800 MHz, achieving 8 TOPS peak throughput, 31.13 TOPS/W energy efficiency, and 14.8 TOPS/mm$^2$ area efficiency, with power consumption ranging from 257 to 272 mW. The design enables on-device training within a sub-100KB on-chip SRAM budget (95KB in silicon).

papers.title: Regret Bounds for Quantum Linear Bandits
papers.abstract: We study $d$-dimensional quantum linear bandits with bounded rewards, where the learner selects an action and queries its quantum reward oracle or its inverse in each round. For general action sets, existing algorithms achieve regret $O(d^{3/2}\operatorname{polylog}(T))$ over $T$ rounds. Prior work established a lower bound of $Ω(d\log(1+T/d))$, leaving open whether the $d^{3/2}$ dependence in the upper bound is necessary. We resolve this question by proving a minimax lower bound of $Ω(d^{3/2}\log(1+T/d^{3/2}))$. To prove this result, we construct a family of hard instances in which the reward gap of each action is proportional to its squared distance from the optimal action. We establish a posterior Fisher information bound for adaptive quantum queries with quantum memory, relating the information acquired about the optimal direction to the regret incurred. Viewing each selected action as an estimate of the optimal direction, we use a matrix Cramér--Rao argument to derive a lower bound on expected regret. When the action set is fixed and has size $K$, we propose two phased elimination algorithms, Soft-G-Elim and QG-Elim. We adapt quantum phase estimation to construct SoftQME, a mean estimator with small bias and controlled tails. Soft-G-Elim estimates the mean reward of every surviving action from independent SoftQME outputs on the support of an experimental design. Controlling the bias and fluctuations of these estimates yields regret $O(d\log T\log(dT)\sqrt{\log(KT)})$, reducing the $\log(KT)\log\log(dT)$ factor in the previous regret bound to $\sqrt{\log(KT)}$. QG-Elim further reduces this factor to $\min\{\sqrt{\log(KT)},\sqrt d\}$.

papers.title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model
papers.abstract: Discrete diffusion generation is emerging as a competitive alternative to autoregressive generation by denoising the entire token sequence through iterative refinement. Its global planning and progressive correction capabilities are particularly well suited to autonomous driving. However, transferring this generation paradigm from general-purpose settings to driving introduces substantial domain gaps in both training and inference. To unlock its potential, we propose a multi-stage optimization pipeline for standard vision-language model architectures, without auxiliary action experts or specialized mixture-of-experts Transformer, spanning post-training and inference. During supervised fine-tuning, we optimize the representation of planning inputs to suppress hallucinations in task responses. During reinforcement learning, we introduce metric-guided diversity filtering to identify stronger learning starting points and improve policy exploration. At inference time, we propose Dynamic Autonomous Driving Decoding (DAD), which adaptively adjusts decoding modes according to scene complexity. Based on this pipeline, we develop Masked Diffusion Drive (MD-Drive), improving its performance by 29.7\% over the unoptimized model. Experiments on the NAVSIM closed loop benchmark and the nuScenes and DriveCoT open loop datasets show that MD-Drive outperforms autoregressive VLM baselines with the same architecture, while achieving a more favorable balance between performance and computational cost than systems with different architectures through discrete diffusion training and inference.

papers.title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
papers.abstract: Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. Reynolds-number-dependent initial conditions are constructed with a boundary layer of Prandtl thickness that converge in the energy norm to an analytic, stationary Euler flow, while the associated Prandtl system develops a finite-time singularity. Highly resolved simulations show boundary-layer detachment and departures from Prandtl scaling, yet provide numerical evidence that the Navier--Stokes solutions continue to converge to the Euler flow over the simulated time interval. In particular, the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and the time-averaged energy dissipation both scale approximately as $Re^{-1/2}$, consistently with established convergence criteria. Although the detached vortices become more numerous and intense as the Reynolds number increases, their characteristic size and occupied area appear to decrease. These observations suggest how boundary-layer detachment and the breakdown of the Prandtl description can coexist with convergence to a smooth Euler flow.

papers.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Dissipativity for Distributed Power-System Stability Analysis
papers.abstract: Compositional dissipativity is attractive for large-scale interconnected systems, but its application to modern heterogeneous power systems is limited by conservative descriptions of nodal dissipativity and inefficient distributed implementation. This paper introduces a common first-order dynamic lifting of the physical voltage-current port, providing an enriched dissipativity representation that captures complementary frequency-dependent energy behavior while preserving network composability. The resulting representation accommodates heterogeneous power system buses within a unified dissipativity description and enables less conservative compositional stability analysis. A centralized stability-certification problem is then formulated and solved through a dual-guided column-generation scheme. Its matrix dual reveals the network-critical dissipation direction, which guides parallel local certificate generation toward the current system bottleneck. This leads to a distributed Network-Critical Margin Exchange (NCME) method with early stability certification. Case studies demonstrate substantially reduced conservatism of the dynamic-port formulation and improved computational and communication scalability of NCME for heterogeneous power systems.

papers.title: KQML-Liver: Interpretable Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Liver Disease Classification
papers.abstract: Liver disease remains a major global health concern, highlighting the need for reliable and accessible early detection methods. Although recent advances in machine learning, deep learning and quantum machine learning (QML) have introduced promising diagnostic tools, many approaches suffer from limited interpretability and inflated performance caused by data leakage or overly simplistic evaluation protocols. These constraints reduce their reliability in real-world clinical practice. This paper proposes KQML-Liver, a hybrid framework that integrates QML with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to enhance predictive performance and interpretability.
