The architecture combines parameterized quantum circuits for expressive feature representation with KAN-based functional mappings that capture nonlinear relationships in an interpretable manner. Evaluated on the Indian Liver Patient Dataset (ILPD) under a rigorous preprocessing protocol preventing data leakage, the proposed model achieves 82% classification accuracy and 100% recall, detecting all positive cases, outperforming existing baselines while providing improved transparency in clinical predictions. These results suggest that hybrid KAN-quantum architectures offer a promising direction for interpretable AI-assisted medical diagnosis.

papers.title: Computational Raga Recognition: A Theory-Driven Approach
papers.abstract: Raga recognition in Hindustani classical music is difficult because a raga is not defined only by the notes used in it. Its identity also depends on the way notes are emphasized, the movement between notes and characteristic phrases. In this work, we develop a computational approach to analyse these characteristics directly from audio recordings. The method uses pitch extracted from recordings and represents it using a 44-position note framework based on the 22-shruti system. From this representation, Raga features based on the Indian classical musicology are extracted.Each feature is compared with a reference representation of the raga and the resulting scores are combined to obtain an overall similarity score. The method is first studied using Raga Yaman and is then tested on recordings of other ragas. The computational results are also compared with the theoretical description of Yaman to identify which raga characteristics are captured well and where the method has limitations.

papers.title: The Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
papers.abstract: We prove the Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $Λ_1\left(Ω\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 λ_1^{\mathrm D}\left(Ω\right)$, where $λ_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{ν,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_ν$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.

papers.title: Small cells in great-circle arrangements
papers.abstract: We study the areas of the cells determined by an arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ of $n$ distinct great circles on the unit sphere, with no three concurrent. Let $m(\mathcal{A})$ and $M(\mathcal{A})$ denote the smallest and largest cell areas, respectively. Our first result is the bound \[ m(\mathcal{A})\le \frac{C_*+O(n^{-3/4})}{n^2}, \qquad C_*=7.0666071493\ldots , \] where the implied constant is absolute. This improves the coefficient $π^2$ obtained from classical polygonal perimeter estimates. We also prove that $M(\mathcal{A})/m(\mathcal{A})>13$ for all sufficiently large $n$, improving the bound $7.43$ of L.~Fejes Tóth. The main tool is a perimeter inequality for planar polygons which takes account of their exterior angles. We combine this with a positive semidefinite kernel on the sphere and use gnomonic projection to obtain bounds for spherical cells.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous First-order Differential Operator Representations of $E_6$ and Graded Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We realize the restricted dual Verma modules of arbitrary highest weight for the complex simple Lie algebra of type $E_6$ by inhomogeneous first-order differential operators in $36$ variables. The construction is obtained by applying Xu's functor (2016) to the full conformal oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{o}(10)$. We construct polynomial bases for all six fundamental $E_6$-modules and obtain a finite spanning set for every finite-dimensional irreducible $E_6$-module $V(λ)$. The degree in $16$ selected variables gives $V(λ)$ a grading over the symmetric algebra of the opposite abelian nilradical. We compute its Hilbert series and graded Betti numbers, and verify the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks conjecture for this family. The minimal graded free resolution of $V(λ)$ is pure precisely when $λ$ is a nonnegative multiple of the Weyl vector of $E_6$. Among nonzero dominant integral $λ$'s, the minimum total Betti number is $435204$, attained exactly at two minuscule weights $ω_1$ and $ω_6$.

papers.title: Dual Representation Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
papers.abstract: The Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is a fundamental and challenging optimization problem in smart manufacturing. Although recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches can learn effective scheduling policies through interaction with the environment, their performance often degrades as problem scale and processing-time uncertainty increase. In this paper, we propose DredRL, a dual representation enhanced diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler. DredRL first constructs enhanced dual representations of operations and machines through self- and cross-attention mechanisms to capture both intra-entity and inter-entity dependencies. A diffusion model is further employed as the policy network, generating scheduling decisions through iterative denoising conditioned on the encoded state to enhance policy expressiveness and robustness. Extensive experiments on synthetic, public, large-scale, and stochastic FJSP benchmarks demonstrate that DredRL outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based schedulers across most configurations. Compared with SOTA learning-based methods, DredRL reduces makespan by up to 5.44% on synthetic instances. It also achieves the best learning-based performance on three of four public benchmarks and outperforms the stochasticity-aware algorithms on stochastic benchmarks. These results demonstrate that combining enhanced dual representations with diffusion-based policies provides an effective and robust approach for large scale scalable FJSP scheduling in complicated environment.

papers.title: Protected Unbiased Sparsification: A Sharp Loewner Curve
papers.abstract: Random sparsification replaces a probability vector by a random vector with few nonzero entries. We ask for unbiasedness, exact preservation of prescribed linear statistics, and a covariance guarantee for every downstream linear response. Let $p$ have $k$ positive coordinates, let $A$ specify the protected statistics, and let $d\le k-2$ be their effective rank. For every $d+1\le m\le k$, we construct an unbiased random probability vector $Q$ with at most $m$ nonzero coordinates, $AQ=Ap$ on every realization, and $\operatorname{Cov}(Q)\preceq h C_{p\mid A}$, where $h=(k-m)/((m-d)(k-d-1))$ and $C_{p\mid A}$ is the categorical covariance after optimal linear adjustment for the protected statistics. This coefficient is sharp uniformly over instances, even among biased estimators when error is measured by its second moment. A residual covariance bridge extends the concurrent unprotected curve to arbitrary pathwise linear protection. We also characterize instance-optimal constants for partitions with uniform weights within classes and derive bounds for peaked weights. For rational inputs, an exact Las Vegas sampler attains the curve within a factor $1+ε$ in expected polynomial time. A separate fast block-pivotal sampler preserves block masses and is no worse in covariance order than independent sampling within blocks. Experiments illustrate the theory on synthetic weights and language-model attention. In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct decoding, the fast sampler preserves block masses, while comparisons with VarOpt remain statistically inconclusive and top-$m$ truncation scores highest on RULER.

papers.title: Multi-dimensional kinetic modeling of laser-plasma instabilities by a Vlasov-Maxwell system
papers.abstract: We present PLAW-EM2d (Two-Dimensional PLAsmaWave ElectroMagnetic Simulation), a two-dimensional Vlasov-Maxwell code for kinetic studies of laser-plasma interactions. The code combines a hybrid electrostatic- TEz field decomposition with an Eulerian 2d2v Vlasov solver for the electron distribution function and a cold closure for the out-of-plane response. Vacuum propagation, Landau damping, and a homogeneousplasma comparison with PIC simulations benchmark the coupled solver. We then consider two representative SRS problems. In an inhomogeneous plasma, the code reproduces convective SRS backscatter with a reflectivity consistent with the Rosenbluth estimate. In a transversely extended target, it captures SRS side scattering in a self-consistent two-dimensional Vlasov simulation, resolving oblique electromagnetic and Langmuir waves that satisfy the resonance conditions. These calculations show that PLAW-EM2d can describe both conventional SRS backscatter and a two-dimensional side-scattering channel relevant to laser-plasma interactions in ICF.

papers.title: Growth function of the cactus groups
papers.abstract: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.

papers.title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
papers.abstract: We introduce the multi-head quantum neural network (QNN), a quantum module compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices that can replace transformer blocks inside pre-trained large language models (LLMs) with little loss in accuracy and with far fewer parameters than the blocks it replaces. Encoding a model's $D$ hidden neurons into a qubit register is the obstacle: amplitude encoding scales poorly in circuit depth and angle encoding in qubit count, so neither is practical at production-scale width. We instead partition the hidden space into $k$ disjoint heads, angle-encode each into an $n_q$-qubit register, process the heads in parallel, and couple them through constrained classical linear layers, the mixers. Performing surgery on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, we show that a single multi-head QNN with $145\,281$ trainable parameters ($D=2048$, $k=32$, $n_q=8$, $L=4$) can replace a contiguous span of eight transformer blocks, displacing $16.33\%$ of the model's parameters. Ablations show that, for a single replaced block, the quantum heads (circuits followed by a learned readout), and not the classical mixers alone, recover the displaced function, whereas for fused spans the mixers alone come within $1$-$3\%$ of the full module in perplexity. Whether this benefit is specific to trained, entangling quantum circuits is not established: controls that switch the entangler off (two seeds), or freeze the circuit at its initial or at uniformly random angles (one seed), beat the full module on held-out perplexity, and a parameter-matched classical multilayer perceptron remains a few percent ahead of the full module. We train classically with exact statevector simulation, then execute the quantum heads of our fusion checkpoints on a $156$-qubit IBM Heron processor, showing that NISQ-scale quantum modules can be installed in a production-scale LLM and run on hardware.

papers.title: Higher order schemes for the numerical solution of integro-differential equation-based age-of-infection models with time-dependent contact rates
papers.abstract: Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging. Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. The resulting numerical schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulations of IDE-based epidemic models with general sojourn time distributions and changing contact patterns.

papers.title: Tau polarization, new physics and CP violation in $ν_τ$-nucleus hyperon production
papers.abstract: Charged-current interactions of the $τ$ neutrino are the least constrained sector of the Standard Model (SM) flavour structure, and the polarisation of the produced $τ$ lepton probes new-physics (NP) couplings, including CP-violating ones. Hyperon and charmed-baryon production gives access to the $u\to s$ and $d\to c$ transitions, but any measurement would be made on nuclei, which calls for a proper treatment of nuclear effects. We therefore study the sequential reactions $ν_τ\,{}^A Z\toτ^-(\toπ^-ν_τ)\,Λ_c^+ X$ and $\barν_τ\,{}^A Z\toτ^+ (\toπ^+\barν_τ)\,ΛX$ within the impulse approximation. The energy and angular distributions of the pion, which encode the $τ$ polarization, are derived for an arbitrary nuclear hole spectral function. As for free nucleons, an azimuthal pion asymmetry with respect to the plane spanned by the neutrino and the outgoing baryon is shown to remain. This is a CP-odd observable that vanishes in the SM, so that a nonzero value would signal CP violation irrespective of the hadronic form factors. Local Fermi gas results for ${}^{16}$O show that nuclear effects lower the reaction thresholds but leave the pion distributions, and hence the polarization information, close to their free-nucleon form. For representative NP scenarios the predicted asymmetries are at the percent level or below, with a magnitude that, in the $Λ$ channel, depends strongly on the transition form factors.

papers.title: Steering Skyrmion Diffusion with Chiral Molecules
papers.abstract: Chiral molecules adsorbed on a magnetic film interact with its magnetization and can thereby alter the thermal motion of magnetic skyrmions. Here we develop a theoretical model in which an aligned layer of tilted molecules modifies the interfacial magnetic interactions according to its handedness. Within this model a skyrmion responds only to spatial variations of the coupling, so a uniform layer leaves its position unaffected, whereas boundaries and coverage gradients exert forces on it. Near a chiral region, these forces deflect the skyrmion transversely in a direction that reverses between enantiomers, which provides a direct signature of the chiral interaction. In extended periodic patterns, the same forces reshape the long-time diffusion, suppressing it in the direction in which the potential varies and enhancing it in the perpendicular direction. The net effect on the mean diffusion is set by the balance between the gyrotropic and dissipative responses of the skyrmion, as we show exactly for one-dimensional landscapes. Stochastic micromagnetic simulations and collective-coordinate calculations confirm these predictions and show how molecular orientation, spatial patterning, and skyrmion properties together determine the motion.

papers.title: Nearly Computable Numbers with Additional Properties
papers.abstract: A real number is called \emph{nearly computable} if it is the limit of a computable sequence of rational (or dyadic) numbers that has the additional property that for any computable subsequence the sequence of differences of consecutive elements converges to $0$ computably. The main result of this article provides methods for constructing nearly computable numbers with additional properties. The main result is proved by an infinite injury priority argument. Using these methods, we construct nearly computable numbers with several different additional properties: - a nearly computable number that is not divergence bounded computable, - for any left-computable number $α$ that is neither in the least nor in the highest Solovay degree, a left-computable, nearly computable number that is Solovay incomparable with $α$, - a nearly computable number $γ$ that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers but has the property that for any two left-computable numbers $α$ and $β$ wih $γ=α-β$ both $α$ and $β$ are Martin-Löf random. We also look at two classes of nearly computable numbers: the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ of differences of real numbers that are nearly computable and left-computable, and the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$ of nearly computable numbers that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers. Both classes form real closed fields, in fact, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is closed under computable functions with open domain that are Lipschitz continuous or differentiable. Finally, we show that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is a proper subset of $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$.

papers.title: Interpreting Selective-Review Coverage for Head-and-Neck Auto-Contours
papers.abstract: Selective-review systems aim to reduce human review by passing candidates predicted to be low risk. However, coverage (the fraction passed) can be misleading when measurements needed to interpret risk are unavailable. We separate structural evaluability (a nonempty mask with all required measurements available), computational-endpoint status, and pass-or-review decisions using archived Mayo records and controlled OpenKBP analyses. In 3,968 Mayo records, all 1,167 recorded empty predictions (predicted target-organ masks containing zero voxels despite nonempty reference masks) were endpoint-negative and passed both modules, accounting for approximately 76% of each pass set. In a held-out OpenKBP test, a logistic-regression router achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.833 and average precision of 0.449 but passed all 544 non-evaluable candidates, including 542 prespecified empty-mask controls and 2 erosions that became empty. A structural gate removed those passes without changing scores or the threshold, preserved all evaluable passes, and assigned 98.71% of endpoint-positive candidates to review. Under the original preprocessing and in patient-disjoint development evaluation, a router trained only on evaluable candidates and a router modeling an unavailable state likewise passed no non-evaluable candidates, with similar evaluable discrimination and at least 99.0% of endpoint-positive candidates assigned to review in pooled outer-fold predictions. These results show that coverage should be interpreted jointly with candidate eligibility, endpoint scope, missingness handling, and routing rules; they do not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or natural-failure prevalence.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes of a Black Hole in a Dehnen-Type Dark Matter Halo with Radial Pressure
papers.abstract: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of scalar and (axial) gravitational perturbations of a black hole spacetime surrounded by a Dehnen-type dark matter (DM) halo with nonvanishing radial pressure. Our results reveal that the real and imaginary parts of the QNMs exhibit distinct redshift coefficients with respect to the DM halo compactness $M/a_0$, in contrast to the vanishing radial pressure case. The magnitude of this effect is dominated by the profile parameter $γ$, and the damping rate is more sensitive to the DM halo compactness than the oscillation frequency. In the eikonal limit, the redshift deviations are well captured by the light ring angular velocity $Ω_c$ and the Lyapunov exponent $λ$.

papers.title: Super Learner: A Practical Tutorial
papers.abstract: The selection of an optimal predictive model is a pervasive challenge in biostatistics and epidemiology. Relying on a single a priori algorithm risks overfitting and reduced generalizability when applied to new settings. Super Learner is a flexible ensemble machine-learning method that mitigates these risks by combining multiple candidate algorithms into a single prediction model. Using cross-validation, it defines a weighted combination of learners that minimizes a specified loss function, ensuring performance asymptotically equal to or better than the best candidate algorithm. This tutorial provides a comprehensive, practical guide to implementing Super Learner in R for applied researchers. Using a simulated epidemiological dataset with a binary outcome, we demonstrate the step-by-step construction of the ensemble. We cover the foundational statistical concepts, basic implementation, evaluation through cross-validation, hyperparameter tuning, feature screening, and performance optimization for metrics such as the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC). Additionally, we detail advanced usage, including computational parallelization and the integration of custom algorithms and screening procedures. The guide also includes a consolidated section on best practices for specifying SL, covering loss function selection, effective sample size determination, CV scheme definition, library curation, and discrete vs. ensemble SL decisions, plus a practical reference to the caret package for model preprocessing and comparison. This guide equips epidemiologists and clinical researchers with the tools to confidently incorporate robust machine learning techniques into their predictive modeling workflows.

papers.title: Exact Decisions and Certified Values in $L_\infty$-Norm Computation from State-Space Representations
papers.abstract: Computing the $L_\infty$-norm of a time-invariant linear ordinary differential control system is a routine task in robust control, usually delegated to floating-point routines that perform well on most practical systems. Behind the numerical value, however, lies a discrete decision: whether a pole lies on the imaginary axis, and whether a mode of a realization is actually a pole of the transfer matrix. Floating-point arithmetic can only replace this decision with a tolerance. This paper explains, for a control audience, what reliable symbolic-numeric computation offers for this problem: exact arithmetic where a decision has to be made, and certified enclosures where a value has to be computed. We show how the problem is turned into a small polynomial system directly from state-space data, how this system is solved in practice, and what it costs. A benchmark on the {\tt COMPleib} library and on families of systems with known norms shows that two standard numerical routines err in opposite directions on the imaginary-axis decision, and never on the same system, while the certified method decides it correctly on every instance tested and computes the norm at a cost comparable to that of the numerical routines on most systems. We conclude with practical guidelines for users of numerical tools.

papers.title: Crystal Nucleation Driven by Microjets from Hydrodynamically Interacting Thermocavitation Bubbles
papers.abstract: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized nucleation mechanism arising from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions using laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs. Under confinement, antiphase generation of two bubbles produces a micron-scale, high-speed liquid jet. Upon impact with the surrounding supersaturated liquid, this microjet generates intense localized shear, thereby inducing crystallization of the model inorganic salt, potassium permanganate. Under identical laser energies and supersaturation levels, crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments, in which no microjet was present. We show that the crystallization probability increases with microjet velocity. Boundary integral simulations reveal how experimental parameters such as confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity. We quantify the relationship between jet velocity and the observed enhancement in crystal nucleation kinetics by incorporating shear into the kinetic prefactor in classical nucleation theory. By combining experiments, theory, and simulations, we establish how microjets emerging from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions may influence crystallization kinetics, opening new opportunities for the manufacture of crystalline materials.

papers.title: Driving World Models Move the Camera, Not the Scene
papers.abstract: Plan-conditioned driving world models are used to compare candidate plans, so their forecast should change with the plan as the real scene would, yet widely used control metrics check only whether the camera follows the command. Recorded drives already contain real outcomes of plans that were never driven: retiming a log gives pose-matched images and LiDAR for other speeds, and a stereo rig records a laterally shifted view. Against these references, released world models move their camera but barely move the scene: their scene response, the share of the real change in distance that the forecast reproduces, reaches at most about a third of real video's, and the trajectory score cannot tell an executed speed command from an ignored one. Interventions inside the generator trace the failure to the plan's channel. The forecast geometry follows the context frames; once they carry the planned geometry, plan tokens add little. ReTime-Compose therefore delivers the plan as geometry, without training. It transports the frames of one logged-speed rollout to the planned cameras, and the frozen model completes only what no frame covers. Frozen generators then follow a 0.54 m lateral shift nearly as the real scene does on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and respond more than re-sampling to slow-down plans in three generators and to speed-up plans in two.

papers.title: Lempert and pluricomplex Green functions near non-semipositive boundary points
papers.abstract: We study the two-step Lempert function and the pluricomplex Green function near a non-semipositive boundary point of a bounded domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove a sharp upper estimate for the two-step Lempert function in terms of the local boundary scale $H_D$, and obtain matching estimates for the pluricomplex Green function. As a consequence, these quantities have the same boundary behaviour as the Kobayashi distance. For the usual Lempert function, we prove an upper estimate of order $\sqrt{H_D}$, which implies the optimal local $1/4$-Hölder estimate, and determine its precise boundary behaviour along the real normal.

papers.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
papers.abstract: Agentic time series forecasting extends conventional approaches beyond one-shot numerical prediction toward autonomous, context-aware interaction. However, existing benchmarks offer limited integrated support for diverse contextual information, forecasting-specific adaptive interactions, and systematic evaluation of forecasting agents. In this paper, we introduce CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting. First, its context-rich dataset suite spans 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets, covering external variables, events, and historical cases under a unified context specification. Second, a lightweight, modular forecasting-native harness provides 49 core tools and a state-adaptive loop that tracks forecast versions and enables iterative evidence gathering and forecast revision. Intermediate forecasts can expose information gaps, while newly acquired evidence guides subsequent revisions and final version selection. Third, model-level evaluation assesses forecast quality, process execution, behavioral trustworthiness, and resource efficiency through decision trajectories and forecast-version histories. Also, systems-level evaluation compares predictive accuracy across forecasting systems. Experiments reveal distinct decision behaviors among agents with comparable accuracy. Additional interactions do not necessarily improve forecasts, and agents may fail to select their best previously generated predictions. Allowing evidence acquisition during forecast refinement improves task-aware forecast scores across all three evaluated models. CastWorld provides a reusable foundation for evaluating agentic time series forecasting under controlled conditions.

papers.title: Probe-Based Routing for Join Optimizer Selection
papers.abstract: In optimizers that choose a join-order solver by a size rule, join ordering is an algorithm-selection problem, because dynamic programming (DP), genetic search (GEQO), and Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) each win on different queries. PostgreSQL nevertheless chooses among them by relation count alone, although queries with the same relation count can favor different solvers. This paper introduces two landscape features that a probe computes from random join orders in microseconds per query. The tail spacing $α$ describes how the costs of the best sampled orders are spaced, and the crossover surprise $θ$ describes how far the cost of a crossover child deviates from the mean cost of its parents. The router clusters training queries by these features and the relation count, assigns a solver to every cluster that this solver wins in total end-to-end time by a margin, and leaves all other queries to PostgreSQL's default rule. On JOB and IMDb-CEB, the router lowers mean end-to-end time relative to the default rule, and on IMDb-CEB the probe features nearly double the gain obtained from the relation count alone, so they carry information about the queries that the relation count lacks.

papers.title: Painlevé XXXIV asymptotics for the defocusing Hirota equation with step-like initial data in transition regions
papers.abstract: We study the long-time asymptotics of the solution of the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with real step-like initial data. Because of the term $α(q_{xx}-2|q|^2q)$, the backgrounds rotate in time, and the symmetry $k\mapsto-k$ of the associated Riemann--Hilbert problem is lost. As a consequence, the branch points $\pm c_l$ and $\pm c_r$ become soft edges along different critical lines. We consider the two transition regions in which the edge $-c_r$, respectively $c_l$, becomes soft, namely the $t^{-2/3}$-neighbourhoods of the lines $x/t=-6βc_r^2+2αc_r$ and $x/t=-6βc_l^2-2αc_l$. By the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method, we show that in both regions the leading correction to the rotating background is of order $t^{-1/3}$ and is a phase correction, in contrast with the order $t^{-2/3}$ known for the defocusing mKdV equation. In the first region, the correction is given by an integral of a solution of the Painlevé XXXIV equation. In the second region, the relevant Painlevé XXXIV model problem reduces to Airy functions, and the correction is a phase shift which is quadratic in $x/t$ and independent of the initial data; in addition, a stationary point of the phase function produces a contribution of order $t^{-1/2}$, which is expressed through parabolic cylinder functions.

papers.title: Quasihyperbolic geodesics in the twice-puntured plane
papers.abstract: We study quasihyperbolic distance and geodesic uniqueness in the plane punctured at 0 and 2. For endpoints on the perpendicular bisector of the punctures and on opposite sides of the real axis, the distance is the smaller of the length of the vertical segment and the least length of a feasible detour. For symmetric endpoints 1 \pm it with t > 0, the geodesic is unique precisely when arsinh t + arctan t < π. At equality there are exactly three geodesic images, and above the threshold there are exactly two. For arbitrary endpoints, we derive variational formulas for the distance in terms of admissible logarithmic spirals and their contacts with the bisector. The minimizing candidates in these formulas give all geodesic images and yield a length-comparison criterion for uniqueness.

papers.title: DaYu-TC: a global-regional nested AI system for tropical cyclone forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate tropical cyclone intensity forecasts are essential for disaster preparedness, yet persistent intensity underestimation limits the value of artificial intelligence (AI) weather models for predicting these destructive storms. Here we present DaYu-TC, a global-regional nested system that links the preservation of strong-wind and low-pressure signals with high-resolution regional prediction. Its global and regional models share an architecture and extreme-aware training objectives. The regional model combines evolving local states with global forecasts valid at each target time, connecting large-scale environmental information with finer-scale cyclone evolution. In an independent evaluation of 16 western North Pacific tropical cyclones in 2023, the global model retains competitive conventional forecast skill while reducing five-day maximum-wind root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 6-22% relative to other evaluated global AI models. Relative to the global model, regional nesting reduces maximum-wind RMSE by 22.0-33.1% and minimum-pressure RMSE by 28.6-39.8% across 12-120 h. The complete system outperforms concurrent operational high-resolution forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts for minimum pressure at 12-120 h and maximum wind speed at 48-96 h, with respective RMSE reductions of 26% and 12% at 72 h. Without retraining, the same regional model enhances three other global AI models, reducing overall maximum-wind RMSE by 22.6-28.6%. Five-day forecasts take under one minute on a single GPU. These results establish a transferable multiscale approach to reducing cyclone intensity underestimation, extending advances in AI weather forecasting towards more accurate prediction of high-impact weather events.

papers.title: A Closer Look at Language Model Introspection: Probing Information and Reporting
papers.abstract: One way to study language-model introspection is to test whether models can identify where their activations have been perturbed. We train a simple linear classifier to identify the perturbed sentence from the model's activations, then compare its predictions with the model's own answers across pretraining and injection strengths. This tests whether the model is being asked to report information that is already easy to recover. If so, successful localization may be less demanding than it first appears and may not extend to the broader uses that motivate introspection research, such as faithfully explaining a model's reasoning or helping researchers assess the reliability of its answers. With an injection four times the typical activation norm at layer 0 and probe readout at layer 24 in OLMo~3 32B, the supervised probe reaches 98.3\% accuracy after 8.4 billion training tokens, while the model's zero-shot answer remains at chance (11.1\%). At the released base checkpoint, these accuracies reach 99.1\% and 89.6\%, respectively. Across 7B and 32B, location is already decodable in randomly initialized networks, showing that the architecture can support these traces without pretraining. In these experiments, location information lies close enough to the surface for a simple linear probe to recover it, so successful reporting need not imply broader access to the model's internal computation.

papers.title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
papers.abstract: Small open models suit private customer-service deployments but trail frontier models in two ways: they miss what the written policy requires in a given situation, and they act inconsistently on what they know. We study whether such a model can close both gaps from its own deployment logs and their reference outcomes, without a stronger teacher model. Our starting point is a Gemma 4 12B agent that reads its domain policy from on-demand skills rather than from its system prompt. In each round, the deployed system serves a fresh batch of tasks; the base model diagnoses failed conversations and writes rules into the skills, and a rule survives only if it passes code checks, counterexample self-review, a paired retest, and a noise-calibrated validation gate. Reinforcement learning (GRPO) then trains a LoRA adapter on complete multi-turn, tool-using conversations. On the retail and airline domains of $τ^2$-bench, without training or selecting on official tasks, the agent after two rounds improves on this starting point by 12.5 pass$^1$ points in retail and 19.5 in airline, and by 18.4 and 22.0 pass$^4$ points. It also exceeds the benchmark's reference agent, which runs the same model with the whole policy in its system prompt, by 11.8 and 8.0 pass$^1$ points and by 22.8 and 16.0 pass$^4$ points, closing most of the gap to three frontier models under the same protocol. A $2\times2$ ablation shows that the rules rescue tasks the agent never solved and carry policy knowledge that RL with the rules in context does not internalize, whereas the trained weights make solved tasks reliable.

papers.title: Extension of the Renard-Deck Drag Decomposition to Compressible Rough-Wall Turbulent Boundary Layers
papers.abstract: A generalized Renard-Deck (RD) drag decomposition is developed for spatially developing compressible turbulent boundary layers over rough surfaces. Derived from the locally resolved, time-averaged momentum equations, the formulation accounts for both viscous friction and pressure drag without requiring spatial averaging at the roughness-element scale. Eight direct numerical simulations are considered at freestream Mach numbers of 2.5 and 5.86, comparing smooth walls and two-dimensional transverse square ribs ($λ_x/k=8$) under adiabatic and cold-wall conditions. The decomposition reconstructs the total drag with errors below 5%. Mean-flow viscous dissipation and turbulent kinetic-energy production together account for approximately 90% of the drag work. While their contributions are comparable over smooth walls, turbulent production dominates over rough walls, contributing approximately 80%. More importantly, roughness substantially alters the wall-normal distributions of both contributions. Viscous dissipation becomes concentrated near the roughness crest, whereas turbulent production peaks above the crest, with both contributions decaying more gradually into the outer layer than over smooth walls. The resulting differences in their cumulative contributions persist across a substantial fraction of the boundary layer, demonstrating that the energetic influence of surface roughness extends well beyond the roughness sublayer.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Multi-View Clustering via View-Aware Quantization
papers.abstract: Federated multi-view clustering (FedMVC) has recently attracted increasing attention for its ability to exploit complementary clustering structures across multiple clients while preserving data privacy. However, existing FedMVC methods often suffer from high communication overhead due to the repeated transmission of high-dimensional representations, which limits their scalability in practical federated systems. Moreover, different views may contribute unequally to the clustering performance, calling for adaptive communication strategies. In this paper, we propose a view-aware quantization algorithm for communication-efficient FedMVC. By dynamically assigning quantization bits based on iteratively updated view importance scores, the proposed algorithm effectively balances clustering performance and communication efficiency under a global bit budget constraint. To validate its generality, we integrate our approach into four state-of-the-art FedMVC methods. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that view-aware quantization achieves up to 6.59x communication reduction while maintaining and in some cases surpassing baseline clustering performance, confirming the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach.

papers.title: MoE Pretraining:Parallelism Layout Changes the Model, Not Quality
papers.abstract: Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are trained across many machines, and the way the work is split, the parallelism layout, often changes between runs: a job resumes on a different GPU count, a cluster is resized, or an ablation runs on a new setup. In exact arithmetic the layout should not matter, but in real arithmetic it changes the order in which numbers are added, and some MoE rules such as load balancing and expert capacity are often computed per machine. We ask whether the layout changes the trained MoE model. We pretrain the same small MoE language models (25M to 117M parameters, 20M FineWeb-Edu tokens) with the same seed, data and hyperparameters under 9 data-parallel and expert-parallel layouts, in fp32 on CPUs and fp16 on a GPU, and compare each run with the effect of a new random seed. Across 80 runs we find: (1) The layout does not change model quality, but it does change the model: final predictions differ about 80% as much as with a new seed, and over 90% of routing decisions differ. Any layout, a one-bit change to one weight, or a different CPU thread count has the same effect. (2) The cause is the router: decisions that flip are almost exactly those where two experts were nearly tied (AUC 0.97 to 1.00 in the first 16 steps). (3) More, smaller experts create more near-ties (2.7% with 8 experts, 23% with 64) and less reproducible routing (68% vs. 100% of decisions differ), but outputs do not drift further. (4) A dense model of the same active size is far more stable (0.12x the seed level in fp32, 0.58x in fp16), while the MoE reaches about 0.8x at both precisions and twice as fast. (5) When pretraining resumes on a new layout, timing matters: switching at 84% of pretraining barely changes the final model, while switching at 10%, just after warm-up, changes it substantially. We release code, run logs and data.

papers.title: Diffuse interstellar bands in nearby galaxies with MaNGA: environmental trends with metallicity, extinction, ionization, and star-forming activity
papers.abstract: Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are absorption features of uncertain origin observed in the optical and near-infrared spectra of stars and galaxies. Although their correlation with dust extinction is well established, the physical conditions governing their strength across different interstellar medium (ISM) environments remain poorly understood. We investigate the environmental dependence of the DIB $\lambda5780$ using spatially resolved MaNGA spectroscopy for 837 nearby galaxies spanning a broad range of stellar masses, star-formation rates, and ISM properties. Stellar and nebular parameters are derived via spectral fitting, while DIB absorption is measured from high-signal-to-noise spatially binned residual spectra. We detect the DIB $\lambda5780$ in 159 galaxies and report the most distant spatially resolved DIB detection to date, at 232 Mpc. The DIB $\lambda5780$ equivalent width correlates positively with both stellar and gas-phase extinction. DIB $\lambda5780$ is preferentially detected in regions of high extinction, near- or super-solar metallicity ($12+\log({\rm O/H})\gtrsim8.5$), and moderate specific star-formation rates ($-10.5\lesssim\log({\rm sSFR}/{\rm yr}^{-1})\lesssim-9$). By contrast, it falls below our detection threshold in metal-poor or strongly ionized environments. It is rarely detected in regions with little or no recent star formation, with the few detections in such environments occurring primarily in regions driven by composite ionization. Our results indicate that DIB $\lambda5780$ is preferentially detected, within the sensitivity limits of the MaNGA data, in dust-rich, chemically evolved, and moderately ionized environments.

papers.title: CP Violation in Beauty Baryon Decays
papers.abstract: The 2025 discovery of CP violation in the baryon sector marks a tectonic shift in flavor physics, bridging a sixty-year gap since the initial discovery of CP asymmetry in mesons. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the theoretical and experimental journey to this milestone. We integrate the development of dynamical calculation frameworks, such as perturbative QCD and the re-scattering mechanism, with the experimental breakthrough achieved through rate asymmetry measurements. Furthermore, we establish a roadmap for the future of the field by detailing the construction of multi-dimensional observables, which are instrumental in advancing the next era of precision physics and refining the search for new physics beyond the standard model.

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Top Taggers from JetClass to a Full-Simulation $Z'\to t\bar{t}$ Search: Transfer, Extrapolation, Sensitivity and Inference Cost
papers.abstract: Searches for heavy resonances decaying to \(t\bar{t}\) test physics beyond the Standard Model at the TeV scale, and their reach depends on how well boosted top jets are identified. Machine-learning top taggers are usually compared on fast-simulation samples without pileup and in a narrow jet-\(p_T\) window, so a benchmark ranking does not directly show how much each tagger adds to a real search. This study trains seven taggers under identical conditions on JetClass. They are a boosted decision tree, two image-based networks, ParticleNet, and three particle transformers (ParT, UParT, and GloParT). The taggers are then applied without retraining to a \(Z'\to t\bar{t}\) search with \(m_{Z'}\) between 1.2 and 2.5~TeV, using 2016 CMS Open Data simulated with Geant4 and realistic pileup. The overall benchmark order of the taggers is preserved. However, taggers with similar area under the ROC curve (AUC) differ by up to a factor of three in jet-level discovery significance. The particle transformers extend the mass reach of the search by \(400~\mathrm{GeV}\), and their lead grows with resonance mass. This gain is seen in fully merged top jets and is associated with stable performance at jet \(p_T\) above the training range. Pileup has only a minor effect on all taggers. A small convolutional network achieves competitive discrimination at a much lower computational cost. The gaps between tagger groups hold under retraining and within statistical uncertainties. The results show that a tagger must be chosen on its kinematic coverage, the working point of the analysis, its discovery sensitivity and its cost, and not on its benchmark score alone.

papers.title: Multicontinuum Poroelasticity Model. Analysis and Computation
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a macroscopic multicontinuum model for Biot poroelasticity. The full macroscopic multicontinuum system is derived by projecting the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces enriched with first-order multiscale corrections. This construction retains generalized pressure storage and coupling terms, with effective coefficients inherited from the microscopic bilinear forms. Under suitable coefficient assumptions, we establish well-posedness and energy stability of the macroscopic multicontinuum model. A fully discrete scheme combining the Galerkin finite element method in space with the backward Euler method in time is then developed. Its well-posedness and stability are proved, and a priori error estimates are derived using appropriate projection operators and energy arguments. Finally, numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate the accuracy of the multicontinuum model with respect to the averaged fine-scale solution.

papers.title: Verify by Doing: Co-Evolving Agent Execution and Evaluation without External Feedback
papers.abstract: Agent self-improvement requires feedback about task success, yet external feedback may be unavailable at test time. Agents must then infer success from observable evidence, and incomplete verification can misguide subsequent updates. We introduce Verify by Doing (VbD), a method that co-evolves Actor and Evaluator harnesses within a single task while keeping model weights fixed. The Evaluator actively inspects artifacts and environment state with tools; its findings ground an internal signal for output selection and guide updates to both execution and verification procedures. Proposed Evaluators undergo comparative review on common candidates, while Actor updates require support from their own fresh outputs. Across AutomationBench, $τ^3$ Banking, and selected GDPval tasks, VbD achieves the highest overall scores among the compared methods operating without external feedback, with gains of 3.3, 4.1, and 2.3 percentage points over the strongest baselines on the main backbone. Ablations support the contributions of active verification and Evaluator evolution, and selection from fixed candidate pools shows that improved verification can recover successful outputs without generating new ones.

papers.title: DroneDiffusion: Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Path Planner for UAV Navigation
papers.abstract: We present DroneDiffusion, a perception-aware diffusion planner for local 3-D UAV trajectory generation that explicitly models and avoids failure zones caused by lens flare, overexposure, and reflective surfaces. A vision-language perceptual safety estimator produces a pixel-aligned reliability map that highlights regions of degraded sensing. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is conditioned on this map together with the onboard RGB image, goal point, and initial velocity to generate egocentric 3-D trajectories. To enforce obstacle avoidance at inference time without retraining, we apply training-free CHOMP guidance over a 3-D Euclidean signed distance field. The model is trained entirely in simulation and deployed zero-shot on a real drone. Reliability conditioning raises the mean perceptual reliability along generated trajectories to 0.71, compared with 0.63 for a geometric baseline, while guidance halves the collision rate of the learned prior from 14.7% to 7.8%. Perceptual safety conditioning and geometric guidance are therefore complementary: treating sensor reliability as a first-class signal reduces incursions into unreliable regions while maintaining competitive navigation performance.

papers.title: PCLSegNet: Anatomy-Aware Deep Learning Framework for MRI-based Pancreatic Cyst Segmentation and Size Assessment
papers.abstract: Early detection and follow-up of pancreatic cystic lesions (PCLs) are crucial, as some of their subtypes, such as mucinous cystic neoplasms (MCNs) and intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, carry a significant risk of malignant transformation. Although most AI studies investigating PCLs rely on computed tomography (CT) scans, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers superior soft tissue contrast, making it highly suitable for PCLs assessment. In this work, we propose an anatomy-aware two-stage deep learning framework for automated PCLs segmentation on abdominal MRI scans. First, a publicly available pancreas segmentation model is used to localize the pancreas. Then, we introduce the anatomyaware PCLSegNet, which incorporates anatomical priors as guidance for pancreas and PCLs segmentation. To address the class imbalance problem, we develop a Class-Specific ErrorWeighted (CSEW) loss function. Postprocessing is applied through anatomical constraints.Our proposed method outperforms multi-organ segmentation models such as TotalSegmentator, achieving substantially higher Dice scores for pancreas segmentation. Moreover, it also achieves a superior normalized surface Dice (NSD) and recall for PCLs segmentationcompared to other state-of-the-art models like nnU-Net, while also notably reducing the false negative rate, facilitating the automatic early detection and the noninvasive imaging-based assessment of PCLs.

papers.title: Can We Ignore Data Dependence in Inference Implementation? A Positive Answer for Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract: In empirical economics, regression discontinuity design (RDD) inference is commonly based on asymptotic normality under an independence assumption, but the running variables or disturbances may exhibit unknown and complex dependence. We first rigorously identify a fundamental dilemma for this conventional practice. To address it, we propose a validity recovery procedure that redefines the roles of bias and stochastic calibration, thereby decoupling data dependence from stochastic calibration. Taking the independence-assumption-based confidence interval as our inferential anchor, our procedure restores its validity while preserving its asymptotic leading constant, even when the data are dependent. For fixed-design RDD based on local linear regression, our intervals achieve asymptotically exact nominal coverage and, compared with the anchor, exploit higher-order smoothness without enlarging the asymptotic variance constant, attaining the minimax-optimal shrinking rates up to a mild factor, such as $\sqrt{\log T})$. The procedure requires neither specific dependence frameworks (e.g., mixing or physical dependence) nor dependence-modeling techniques (e.g., long-run variance estimation). For random-design RDD, under more specific dependence assumptions, we derive the rate-explicit coverage error at each nominal level and characterize the trade-off between this rate and interval length. Moreover, modeling dependence becomes an optional enhancement that can further enable validity recovery and improve finite-sample coverage, while averaging over repeated calibrations stabilizes the randomized center and protects against undercoverage in finite samples without increasing interval length. In short, under mild dependence and moment conditions, our procedure makes data independence an implementation default rather than a validity requirement. Simulations support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
papers.abstract: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.

papers.title: Priority-Based Network Access with Strict-Priority Scheduling in PLCA Multidrop Networks
papers.abstract: Shared-medium Ethernet is gaining renewed attention across industrial domains, driven by the adoption of 10BASE-T1S. In such multidrop networks, collision-free and deterministic medium access is achieved through Physical Layer Collision Avoidance (PLCA). However, PLCA follows a node-based cyclic access structure that does not account for traffic priority, leading to high access latency for time-sensitive traffic and limited scalability with increasing network size. Existing PLCA extensions improve latency for selected devices but remain restricted to node-based access and do not support network-wide traffic differentiation. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a priority-based network access and scheduling mechanism for multidrop networks. The proposed approach decouples medium access from node-based ordering and enables class-based prioritization, allowing high-priority traffic from any device to be transmitted ahead of lower-priority traffic. It further supports a configuration that emulates Strict Priority (SP) scheduling, providing low and bounded access latency for highest-priority traffic. Analytical bounds on the worst-case access latency are derived, validated, and shown to be tight. Performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed mechanism reduces the maximum observed access latency for high-priority traffic by over 65% compared to PLCA, with latency increasing by less than 1% as the network grows from 8 to 40 devices.

papers.title: Sharp Liouville theorems for the Hardy-Hénon p-Laplace equation and classification of positive solutions for the critical Hardy p-Laplace equation
papers.abstract: We prove subcritical nonexistence for $-Δ_pu=|x|^au^q$ in $R^N$, with $1<p<N$ and $a>-p$, in the positive locally bounded weak class. Continuous Steiner symmetrization of a nonlinear auxiliary potential yields a directional pressure inequality; a localized Pohozaev identity and scaling give the Liouville theorem. At criticality, for $N\ge3$ and $-p<a<0$, we classify all positive entire weak solutions in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(R^N)$, without assuming local boundedness, symmetry, stability, finite energy, or decay at infinity.

papers.title: Device-independent witnesses of genuine multipartite entanglement and nonlocality for GHZ states and Bell-pair tree
papers.abstract: We derive and compare device-independent witnesses of genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) and genuine multipartite nonlocality (GMNL) for GHZ states and trees of Bell pairs. A binary-outcome family using four global measurement contexts has the tight biseparable bound independent of the number of parties. We distinguish these GME bounds from Svetlichny-hybrid bounds, which permit arbitrary communication within either side of a bipartition. For GHZ states, we also give a $2N$-context GMNL witness and compare it with MABK and Svetlichny tests. For Bell-pair trees, sums of CHSH and chained inequalities certify GME and GMNL, respectively, with explicitly specified input protocols and multi-bit local outputs. Separately, we prove the sharp four-context network bound $I_λ\leq2$ for every $N\geq3$ and $λ\geq2$, and bound the MABK scores of quantum networks assembled from bipartite sources. We successfully benchmark MABK, four-context, and Svetlichny witnesses on IBM Quantum GHZ preparations up to $10$ parties, under the local-measurement and sampling assumptions.

papers.title: A hybrid machine learning-analog framework for downscaling unprecedented climate extremes
papers.abstract: Extreme weather events are critical for climate impact assessments. While physical models can simulate unprecedented extremes, for example, through ensemble boosting, this approach is computationally demanding, often restricting output to coarse spatial resolutions. Probabilistic generative downscaling offers a solution by enabling efficient sampling from the entire climate distribution, including its extreme tails. Here, we first demonstrate that machine learning generated regional climate model heatwaves over Paris are physically realistic. We then leverage an emulated machine learning dataset to perform analog-based downscaling of coarse global climate model ensemble boosting events. Our hybrid framework effectively bridges high-resolution regional detail with rare-event sampling, providing an efficient tool for extreme event downscaling and capturing multi-model uncertainty.

papers.title: Multi-Band Indoor MIMO Channel Measurements Across Sub-6 GHz, Mid-Band and mmWave: Comparing 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz
papers.abstract: Future wireless systems for indoor applications are expected to extend their operating frequencies from sub-6 GHz to mid-band and millimeter wave (mmWave) frequencies to support higher data rates. To characterize the frequency-dependent propagation behavior across these bands, multi-band channel measurements are essential. In this work, we conduct double-directional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel measurements in an indoor environment to enable a consistent comparison across three frequency bands. Measurements are performed using a 16x16 MIMO configuration at center frequencies of 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz, covering both line-of-sight (LOS) and obstructed line-of-sight (OLOS) conditions. The measured channels are processed using the space-alternating generalized expectation maximization (SAGE) algorithm to extract multipath parameters, which are subsequently used to characterize the angular power distributions across the three frequency bands. The results show substantial angular-domain similarity across all three bands in both LOS and OLOS conditions, while also highlighting frequency-dependent variations.

papers.title: Multi-Label Classification with Constrained Search for Inverse Design of a 16x16 Reconfigurable Pixel Antenna
papers.abstract: In this paper, an inverse design method is presented for a 16x16 reconfigurable pixel antenna with 480 binary switches, giving 2480 possible patterns, far beyond what full-wave simulation can explore. Given a target frequency between 1 and 6 GHz, the method searches for a switch configuration whose simulated resonance lies close to the target. A forward surrogate model is trained on 22,152 full- wave simulated patterns to predict where a given switch pattern resonates. The forward task is formulated as multi-label classification over 100 frequency bins rather than reflection-coefficient regression, because a curve-fitting objective is dominated by the flat baseline around the narrow resonances of this structure. The inverse design is a simulated annealing search over the switch state, with a connectivity constraint maintained at every step so that every pattern generated is a valid antenna. The proposed methodology combines resonance-focused surrogate modelling with connectivity-constrained discrete optimization, enabling candidate generation without full-wave solver calls during the search. The pipeline is verified in CST Microwave Studio by simulating 220 predicted candidates, ten for each of 22 target frequencies. For each request, the best of the ten candidates reached a median frequency error of 23 MHz across the 22 targets, compared with 35 MHz for a solver-guided search using 200 simulations for each target. The proposed methodology therefore enables automatic switch configuration to achieve a requested resonant frequency, eliminating solver calls during the search and manual redesign of the antenna geometry.

papers.title: Track4D: Representing Dense 3D Tracking for Video Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We study how to repurpose video diffusion models (VDMs), pretrained on millions of videos, for dense 3D point tracking, where training data is scarce. Doing so is non-trivial, as it requires representing 3D tracks as video-like signals that may lie outside the natural-video distribution on which the VDM was trained. We thus systematically assess the effectiveness of two such video representations. The first, Residual 3D Tracking Video (RTV), encodes per-pixel 3D offsets relative to a query frame and allows recovery of 3D trajectories directly from the generated video. The second, Normalized Coordinate Map Video (NCMV), labels each pixel with a canonical coordinate invariant through time. This is closer to a natural video and easier for the VDM to learn, but requires additional post-processing with an off-the-shelf 2D tracker to recover 3D tracks. RTV tracks more accurately, while NCMV shows that a VDM can generate dense correspondence as a video. We instantiate both representations with LoRA adaptation of a frozen Wan backbone, conditioned on point maps from an off-the-shelf 3D reconstructor as a geometric scaffold. Trained with a single dynamic 3D tracking dataset, Track4D achieves competitive zero-shot tracking on four real and synthetic benchmarks. A regression readout that bypasses the video VAE and uses additional training data brings further improvement, demonstrating the potential of this direction for dense 3D tracking. We hope our analysis will inspire future work that leverages VDM priors for dense 3D tracking and 4D reconstruction. Project page: https://nirvanalan.github.io/projects/track4d

papers.title: FineSpeaker: Reliable Speaker Representation Learning at Fine Temporal Resolution
papers.abstract: Speaker representation learning is fundamental to speech processing tasks such as speaker verification and diarization. Although long-context speaker encoders can produce stable and discriminative embeddings, short-duration verification and diarization require finer-grained temporal representations. Short temporal contexts limit the available speaker evidence and make speaker identity difficult to disentangle from phonetic and acoustic variability. This creates a temporal resolution-representation reliability trade-off: speaker representations should maintain local within-speaker consistency, between-speaker discriminability and remain sensitive to speaker changes at fine temporal resolution. Accordingly, we propose a framework for reliable speaker representation learning at fine temporal resolution. FineSpeaker first constructs resolution-controllable frame-wise speaker representations through mean pooling over an adjustable n-frame window, enabling flexible control of representation granularity. It then introduces a speaker encoder with local temporal modeling that exploits short-range speaker context to improve the stability and discriminability of short-duration and frame-wise representations. Furthermore, we develop a generative disentanglement strategy for optimizing frame-level speaker representations, combining VAE-based probabilistic modeling with flow matching to characterize speaker-related variation and suppress non-speaker interference. Experiments demonstrate competitive full-utterance performance, improved fine-grained speaker verification on VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb, and strong zero-shot diarization results, highlighting the benefits of balancing temporal resolution and representation reliability.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Data-Driven Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) has attracted substantial interest, and many variants have been proposed; however, comparatively less is known about the statistical closed-loop performance of these methods and the fundamental limits they are subject to. In this contribution, we apply the statistical decision framework developed in our earlier work to study fundamental limits of DDPC. The performance of a data-driven controller is measured by its risk, the expected deterioration in control performance relative to an oracle model-based controller at a given system, and by its total risk that measures the overall performance across all systems of interest. Lower bounds on these risks are derived using the bias-variance decomposition and the Cramer-Rao inequality. In particular, a lower bound on the total risk is obtained by a calculus-of-variations method. This bound applies to any DDPC design, thereby quantifying unavoidable performance limitations and providing a benchmark for assessing existing DDPC methods. In an illustrative example, we compare the risks of certainty-equivalence model predictive control, subspace predictive control, and data-enabled predictive control with the derived lower bounds, providing a quantitative performance assessment of these methods and some guidance on tuning regularization parameters in DDPC.

papers.title: Hypersonic Flow Over an Axisymmetric Open Cavity: Effects of Segmentation Angle and Reynolds Number
papers.abstract: This study investigates the influence of cavity segmentation angle ($φ$) on the flow characteristics of a cavity mounted on a cone under Mach 6 freestream conditions in a Ludwieg tunnel. Four segmentation configurations, corresponding to $φ= 360^\circ$, $48^\circ$, $32^\circ$, and $16^\circ$, are examined for cavity length-to-depth ratios ($L/D$) of 1 and 6 over a range of Reynolds numbers ($Re_D = 23000$--$74000$). The flow field is characterized using surface pressure and heat flux measurements, complemented by planar laser Rayleigh scattering visualization. The results indicate that, for $L/D = 1$, the downstream Strouhal number ($St$) and mean pressure remain largely unaffected by the segmentation angle and closely agree with those of the axisymmetric configuration. In contrast, the flow parameters within the cavity are larger than in the axisymmetric case, which is attributed to the three-dimensional bounding effect. For $L/D = 6$, the mean pressure distribution exhibits a similar trend across the segmentation angles, whereas the downstream $St$ increases with increasing $φ$, approaching the axisymmetric value. Flow-mode transitions are observed across all segmentation angles, consistent with the axisymmetric configuration. However, both the transition Reynolds numbers and the corresponding flow modes vary with the segmentation angle.

papers.title: Learning Rate Transfer and Feature Learning Across Depth for Constrained Spectral Optimizers: Complete Scion
papers.abstract: Hyperparameter transfer across model depth is instrumental in training deep models, as it enables learning rates calibrated on shallow networks to be effectively applied to deeper architectures. The recent CompleteP framework establishes a $1/L$ residual scaling rule that demonstrates this for Adam-family optimizers. We study whether similar transfer extends to constrained optimization methods, specifically Frank-Wolfe and projected non-Euclidean normalized steepest descent, where updates are determined by linear minimization oracles. We derive scaling rules for these methods which confirm that the $1/L$ residual scaling applies, although the arguments differ from the Adam-family optimizers. Our analysis supports depth-wise transfer and width-wise transfer of the learning rate for the Scion algorithm while ensuring feature learning and avoiding the kernel-regime. In experiments on NLP transformers (nanoGPT on FineWeb), vision transformers (DeiT on ImageNet), and vision MLPs (MLP-Mixer on CIFAR-10), we observe learning rate transfer across depth and feature learning for appropriately chosen residual scaling.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of a Dual-Polarised Bowtie Antenna in the Low RF Band: A Low-Cost Undergraduate Laboratory Experiment
papers.abstract: We have set up a simple experiment to characterise a dual-polarised bowtie dipole antenna at St. Stephens College as part of undergraduate radio astronomy experiments. The antenna provides two orthogonal linear polarisation responses, allowing us to investigate the polarisation properties of radio-frequency signals using a simple and affordable experimental setup. In this article, we present our analysis of the performance of the antenna and demonstrate its use through polarisation-rotation measurements. This antenna is part of the Sky Watch Array Network (SWAN) and this analysis helps us understand the response of each individual array element in the setup.

papers.title: Cross-channel amplification of frequency-distinct scattered waves in multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering
papers.abstract: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) can be amplified when one side-scattered wave draws energy from several pumps, each through a separate ion-acoustic-wave (IAW) branch. This is not common-daughter-wave coupling: scattered waves from different parent pumps may occupy nearly the same wave-vector region yet remain distinct optical modes because their frequencies differ. We examine this process with local-growth and finite-width-gain models, three-dimensional coupled-mode calculations and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. Adding the extra branches increases temporal growth and spatial gain across the tested crossing angles. In three dimensions, direct branches alone give weak, localized side scatter; with the cross branches present, a strong field fills much of the interaction region even though the incident beams, direct channels and initial seed are unchanged. The distinction persists at fixed total power. The coupled response remains strong as the power per beam falls, whereas the direct-only response drops rapidly. PIC spectra contain nearby scattered-light features accompanied by several pump-specific IAW branches, and the fixed-power scans yield a strong, non-monotonic response. These results support cross-channel feedback through separate IAWs as a multibeam SBS amplification mechanism that may help predict and control SBS losses in laser-fusion plasmas.

papers.title: On shared responsibility, fish, and the strong law of large numbers
papers.abstract: We give a new, short, and intuitive proof of the strong law of large numbers for i.i.d. random variables.

papers.title: Statistical Characterization of CME Interaction Responsible for Successive Type II Solar Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: Successive type II solar radio bursts are often considered as diagnostics for the evolution of CME-driven shocks and their interaction with the structured solar corona. However, the physical mechanisms driving these successive type II emissions are not well understood, with prior studies mostly limited to single event. In this work, we provide the first statistical analysis of successive type II radio bursts over Solar Cycles 23, 24 and the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25 (1997-2025). We have constructed a catalogue of 73 independent successive type II events using radio dynamic spectra and SOHO LASCO coronagraph observations. The events were divided into three observational classes, based on the inferred physical interaction mechanisms: CME-Streamer interaction, CME-CME interaction and Single-CME. Statistical analyses were performed on the 56 events with clear physical classification. CME-streamer interactions constitute the largest class among the physically classified event, highlighting the potential importance of the ambient coronal environment in shaping successive type II radio emission. Comparative statistical analyses indicate that the CME linear speed has marginal differences among the physical classes, but the CME angular width is significantly different between the CME-CME and CME-Streamer populations. Other factors, such as shock evolution and the ambient coronal environment, are important for the production of successive type II radio burst. The catalogue presented here provides a statistical framework for the investigation of CME-driven shock evolution.

papers.title: APG-Planner: Learning Vision-Based High-Speed Trajectory Planning via Analytic Policy Gradient
papers.abstract: Vision-based high-speed navigation requires a trajectory planner that can reactively generate smooth, collision-free trajectories from onboard visual observations. Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to vision-based trajectory planning, as it enables the optimization of sequential decision-making policies in complex environments. However, model-free policy gradient methods rely on sample-based policy gradient estimation, which yields noisy gradient estimates and inefficient training. To this end, we propose a framework for learning trajectory planning policies using the analytic policy gradient (APG) method and use it to train APG-Planner, a vision-based high-speed trajectory planner. The proposed framework leverages differential flatness to analytically reconstruct vehicle states from planned trajectories, thereby enabling differentiable trajectory-level state transitions without requiring an explicit low-level dynamics model. By iteratively performing trajectory planning and differentiable state transitions, we construct a differentiable episode rollout and analytically compute policy gradients from episode-level losses, improving both training efficiency and policy performance. After approximately 30 minutes of training on a single GPU, APG-Planner demonstrates comparable or superior performance to existing baseline methods in simulation and achieves speeds of up to 11\,m/s in real-world flight experiments. We further validate the proposed framework on a skid-steer ground robot, demonstrating its applicability to differentially flat robotic systems beyond quadrotors.

papers.title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
papers.abstract: The function of oxide materials, from solid-oxide fuel cells to solar thermochemical fuel production, depends on their oxygen vacancies. Their formation energetics have been mapped systematically for ternary perovskites, but reported values for the binary oxides, their conceptual and thermochemical building blocks, remain scattered across studies with differing computational methods. Here we report a systematic r$^2$SCAN density functional theory survey of neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies across 39 binary main-group metal oxide polymorphs spanning groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15, using the ShakeNBreak method to locate reconstructed defect ground states. The formation energies span 8 eV and decrease down each group and, for most multivalent cations, with increasing oxidation state. Both trends follow the reducibility of the cation. An interpretable crystal feature model is fit to these energies; its inputs are properties of the pristine bulk, with the reduction potential alternatively taken from tabulated thermochemistry. Retaining only its two dominant descriptors, the crystal reduction potential and the band gap, the model reproduces the formation energies with a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV, lower than that of its four-descriptor parent model for transition-metal perovskites. The bond-breaking and stability terms of the full Born-Haber fit prove statistically null for the binary oxides, and the largest residuals identify the hosts where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture that the descriptors encode. The dataset provides a benchmark for machine-learning interatomic potentials, and the model estimates vacancy formation energies of main-group oxides from bulk properties alone.

papers.title: Quantum Recurrent Architectures for Financial Time Series Prediction
papers.abstract: This study evaluates quantum classical hybrid recurrent architectures for financial time-series forecasting: a Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) network and Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) with lag-based inputs.
